143944	For patients with chronic obstructive airways disease ( COAD ) admitted to hospital in ventilatory failure , mortality ranges from 6% to 34% , the most reliable predictors of mortality being increased age and respiratory acidosis .
143945	Nasal intermittent positive pressure ventilation ( NIPPV ) has been used in patients with acute and chronic respiratory failure due to neuromuscular disease , chest wall deformities , COAD , cystic fibrosis , and obstructive sleep apnoea .
143946	In a small controlled study , Ahmed et al showed an improved outcome for patients with COAD treated with NIPPV compared with the respiratory stimulant doxapram .
143947	We have compared NIPPV with conventional treatment in patients admitted to hospital with ventilatory failure due to acute exacerbations of COAD .
143948	Patients and methods
143949	After ethical committee approval , we did a randomised controlled trial at King 's College Hospital , Southampton General Hospital , and the London Chest Hospital ( centres A , B , and C ) .
143950	Patients gave informed consent , or if they were too ill to cooperate , the consent of a relative was obtained .
143951	Patients admitted with an acute exacerbation of COAD and who were aged 80 or less , had an arterial PaO 2 &lt;7.5 kPa , and an arterial PaCO 2 &gt;6 kPa , were eligible for inclusion .
143952	Patients were excluded if they had severe disease not attributable to chronic respiratory disease , severe psychiatric disease , or if they used NIPPV at home .
143953	Patients were randomly allocated to receive either conventional treatment alone ( control group ) , or conventional treatment plus nasal intermittent positive pressure ventilation ( NIPPV group ) .
143954	Conventional treatment was that deemed appropriate by the clinicians responsible : oxygen at 24–28% ; inhaled bronchodilators ; and all , or a combination of , antibiotics , diuretics , respiratory stimulants , intravenous or oral corticosteroids , and bronchodilators .
143955	Patients were assessed and treated as necessary by a physiotherapist .
143956	Volume-cycled nasal positive pressure ventilation was started as soon as possible in the NIPPV group with either a Lifecare PLV 100 ( Lifecare , Lafayette , Colorado , USA ) in the assist-control mode , or a Brompton-PAC ( PneuPAC Ltd , Luton , Beds , UK ) .
143957	Ventilation was through a silicone nasal mask ( Respironics Ltd , Murrysville , Pennsylvania , USA ; UK distributors : Medicaid , Pagham , Sussex ) with O 2 at 1–2 L/min .
143958	The ventilated group were encouraged to use NIPPV for up to 16 h per day , including all night , with ventilation discontinued for eating , drinking , and moving around .
143959	As the patients improved , the duration of NIPPV was reduced , at first during the day , and then at night .
143960	Arterial blood gases were measured on admission , after 1 h on allocated treatment , on day 3 , and day 7 , while breathing room air ( except at 1 h after admission when the patient was using either O 2 or NIPPV ) .
143961	Visual analogue scores ( VAS ) for shortness of breath , well-being , and quality of sleep were obtained from the patients ; and for nursing care requirements from a senior nurse , daily until day 3 , and then on day 7 .
143962	FEV 1 , FVC , and peak expiratory flow rate were measured during the hospital stay .
143963	Patients were followed-up for at least 30 days .
143964	Ventilation was started and VAS measured by physiotherapists and medical researchers not otherwise involved in the management of the patients .
143965	Statistics
143966	Arterial blood gas measurements were compared in the two treatment groups with unpaired t-tests on differences , and between the three centres using analysis of variance .
143967	The VAS were averaged over the first 3 days of admission ( any patient with data missing was omitted from the analysis ) and these means compared by Mann-Whitney U tests .
143968	Proportions of patients surviving 30 days were compared with Fisher 's exact test .
143969	Results
143970	Patients and treatments
143971	60 patients were entered in the trial : approximately 10 in each group at each of the 3 centres .
143972	The 2 groups had similar ages , arterial blood gases , and spirometry .
143973	Patients at centre C were less acidotic ( pH 7.369 [ SD 0.043 ] ) , than the patients at A , ( pH 7.340 [ SD 0.065 ] ) , and B ( pH 7.310 [ SD 0.087 ] ) , p &lt; 0.05 .
143974	Mean PaO 2 and PaCO 2 were no different .
143975	Although patients at centre C had a somewhat lower PaCO 2 ( mean 8.2 kPa [ SD 1.24 ] ) , compared with centre A ( 8.7 kPa [ SD 1.65 ] ) , and centre B ( 8.9 kPa [ SD 1.67 ] ) .
143976	Of the 30 patients randomised to NIPPV , 4 did not receive it : 2 because they were confused and could not cooperate , 1 because he was unable to breathe through his nose , and 1 because he requested the withdrawal of all active treatment .
143977	5 patients allocated conventional treatment were ventilated on the decision of the clinician in charge : 3 Figure 2 — Mean visual analogue scores.received NIPPV , and 2 were intubated ( 1 of whom died ) .
143978	All patients received controlled O 2 and nebulised bronchodilators , and about 75% of patients in both groups received corticosteroids and antibiotics .
143979	In the NIPPV group , 18 ( 60% ) were given diuretics , 7 ( 23.3% ) methylxanthines , and 4 ( 13.3% ) doxapram .
143980	In the control group , 13 ( 43.3% ) were given diuretics , 14 ( 46.7% ) methylxanthines , and 13 ( 43.3% ) doxapram .
143981	The 26 NIPPV patients received 7.63 ( 1–23 ) h of ventilation day , over 6.0 ( 2–9 ) days , taking 1.86 ( 0.25–4 ) h to settle on ventilation .
143982	Median stay in hospital was 9 ( 1–39 ) days for the control group and 9 ( 1–22 ) days for the NIPPV group .
143983	Arterial blood gases
143984	There was a mean rise in pH in the NIPPV group from 7.348 to 7.376 , and a mean fall in pH in the control group from 7.331 to 7.313 after one hour of treatment .
143985	This was a mean difference in change of 0.046 ( CI=0.06 to 0.02 , p &lt; 0.001 ) ( fig 1 ) .
143986	PaCO 2 in the NIPPV group fell from 8.6 kPa to 7.3 kPa ; and in the control , from 8.6 kPa to 8.5 kPa .
143987	This was a mean difference in change of 1.2 kPa ( CI=0.45 to 2.03 , p &lt; 0.01 ) .
143988	There was no statistically significant difference in arterial blood gas measurements between the two groups during the rest of the admission , although the values of the control group tended to be more variable for both pH and PaCO 2 .
143989	Symptoms and nursing care
143990	Visual Analogue Scores over the first 3 days showed a significantly lower score for breathlessness for the NIPPV group , median 2.3 cm ( range 0.1–5.5 ) , than for the control group , median 4.5 cm ( range 0.9–8.8 ) , p &lt; 0.025 ( fig 2 ) .
143991	The VAS of quality of sleep and general well-being , and for the amount of nursing care required , were not statistically significantly different .
143992	Survival
143993	Survival rates at 30 days were compared for an intention-to-treat and an efficacy population .
143994	In the NIPPV group , mortality within 30 days was less than with the conventional treatment group : 1/26 vs 9/30 ( relative risk=0.13 , CI=0.02 to 0.95 , p=0.014 ) .
143995	However , when analysed on an intention-to-treat basis with inclusion of the 4 patients who were not treated with NIPPV , 2 of whom died , the survival advantage was lower : 3/30 vs 9/30 ( relative risk=0.33 , CI=0.10 to 1.11 , p=0.106 ) .
143996	Short-term survival differed between the centres .
143997	In the first 30 days there were no deaths at centre C , 5 at B , and 7 at A ( centre C vs centre A and B : Fisher 's exact test p=0.005 ) .
143998	One patient ( centre B ) continued with NIPPV at home and remains well .
143999	Patients who subsequently died were more acidotic on admission than patients who survived : pH 7.310 ( SD 0.078 ) vs pH 7.347 ( SD 0.067 ) ( p=0.01 ) ; and more hypercapnic : PaCO 2 9.4 kPa ( SD 1.45 ) vs 8.4 kPa ( SD 1.51 ( p &lt; 0.05 ) .
144000	Both groups were equally hypoxic , PaO 2 5.1 kPa ( SD 0.93 ) and 5.3 kPa ( SD 1.05 ) .
144001	Discussion
144002	Blinding in this study was impossible , as ‘ sham ’ ventilation with NIPPV can not be done .
144003	To minimise potential bias , the study investigators set up the ventilators but were not involved in the clinical management of patients .
144004	There was a rapid improvement in pH and PaCO 2 for the NIPPV group , and for the first 3 days they were less short of breath than the control group .
144005	Although many patients were unable to complete a VAS on the day of admission , it is unlikely that the NIPPV group were less breathless as the groups were otherwise well matched .
144006	Sequential data were not available for the patients in the control group who were intubated and ventilated , nor for the NIPPV patients who could not be treated with nasal ventilation .
144007	Comparison of arterial blood gas tensions and VAS necessarily , therefore , excluded the most sick patients in the conventionally treated group .
144008	This may have masked further treatment benefits of NIPPV .
144009	Comparison of the data for the 26 patients who received NIPPV with that of the 30 treated conventionally demonstrated improved survival ( 1 death in 26 vs 9 in 30 ) .
144010	Analysed on an intention-to-treat basis the mortality of the two groups ( 3/30 vs 9/30 ) was not significantly different .
144011	The mortality in patients randomised to receive conventional treatment alone , 9/30 ( 30% ) , was higher than in some previous reports .
144012	The criteria for inclusion in the study ensured that all patients had severe COAD with ventilatory failure , and so could be expected to have a substantial mortality .
144013	Centre C had no deaths during the study .
144014	The patients at this centre were less acidotic on admission , indicating that they were less critically ill at the start of the study .
144015	This may reflect differences in hospitals rather than patients since centre C has no casualty department and most patients are admitted direct to the ward .
144016	Jeffrey et al have suggested that doxapram should be given to all patients who are acidotic and hypercapnic , although Ahmed et al found a poor outcome in 5 patients treated with doxapram in a controlled study comparing doxapram with NIPPV .
144017	Patients in our study fared better with NIPPV , and in the conventional treatment group ( 43% of whom received doxapram ) some patients had to switch to NIPPV .
144018	Although the application of NIPPV on a general ward has been described as a difficult and time-consuming procedure for nurses we did not find this to be the case .
144019	We conclude that this treatment should be offered to patients with an acute exacerbation of COAD who are acidotic and hypercapnic , compliant , with no nasal abnormality and in whom conventional therapy does not produce a prompt response .
144020	This study was supported by a grant from the British Lung Foundation .
144021	A table of patients ' results is available from the corresponding author
144022	Placebo-controlled trial of essential fatty acid supplementation in atopic dermatitis
144023	Treatment of atopic dermatitis with essential fatty acids remains controversial .
144024	A double-blind , placebo-controlled , parallel-group study was done to investigate the response of patients with atopic dermatitis to essential fatty acid supplements .
144025	Patients with atopic dermatitis were randomised to receive evening primrose oil , evening primrose oil and fish oil , or placebo for 16 weeks .
144026	Disease activity was monitored by clinical severity scores recorded by the investigator , topical steroid requirement , and symptom scores recorded by subjects .
144027	Of 123 subjects recruited , 102 completed the treatment period .
144028	No improvement with active treatment was demonstrated .
144029	Our study , which avoided the methodological and analytical problems of previous studies , found no effect of essential fatty acid supplementation in atopic dermatitis .
144030	Introduction
144031	Evening primrose oil contains n6 series essential fatty acids ( EFAs ) .
144032	Epogam , a product containing this oil , is widely prescribed in the UK for treatment of atopic dermatitis ( AD ) .
144033	Clinical trials of evening primrose oil in AD have been inconclusive , and the use of fish oil , a source of n3 series EFAs , to treat AD has also yielded conflicting results .
144034	The possible mechanisms by which EFAs might improve inflammatory skin disease include modification of eicosanoid metabolism so as to favour synthesis of relatively non-inflammatory prostaglandins and leukotrienes .
144035	Since both n6 and n3 EFAs may possess this property , it is possible that giving both together will have a synergistic effect .
144036	Our study was designed to investigate whether evening primrose oil was effective in AD , and whether any additional response might be gained from the simultaneous administration of fish oil .
144037	Patients and methods
144038	Patients
144039	The study had a double-blind , randomised , parallel-group design with three treatment limbs .
144040	Subjects were examined at baseline , at 4 , 8 , and 16 weeks on treatment , and again after an 8 week washout .
144041	Outpatients attending the dermatology department for treatment of AD , of either sex and all ages , were recruited .
144042	The diagnostic criteria of Hanifin and Rajka were used .
144043	To avoid a disparity in age distribution between treatment groups , adults and children aged up to 12 years were randomised separately in blocks of three .
144044	Equal numbers of adults and children were recruited .
144045	All gave written informed consent .
144046	Treatments
144047	Patients were randomised to receive epogam , Efamol Marine , or matching placebo ( Scotia Pharmaceuticals Guildford , UK ) .
144048	Epogam capsules contained 500 mg of evening primrose oil , largely made up of the n6 series EFAs linoleic ( 321 mg ) and gamma-linolenic acid ( 40 mg ) .
144049	Efamol marine capsules contained 430 mg of evening primrose oil and 107 mg of marine fish oil .
144050	This fish oil included the n3 series EFAs eicosapentaenoic acid ( 17 mg ) and docosahexaenoic acid ( 11 mg ) .
144051	Placebo capsules contained liquid paraffin for adults and olive oil for children .
144052	Six capsules of each treatment were given twice daily for 16 weeks .
144053	Capsules were cut open , if necessary , to administer the contents to children .
144054	Compliance was monitored by questioning patients and counting remaining capsules at each outpatient visit .
144055	Patients taking less than 70% of their capsules ( 50% for children ) were defined as non-compliers .
144056	Patients were allowed to use topical steroids and emollients as required .
144057	They were advised to use topical steroids only on severely affected areas of skin , in accordance with our usual practice .
144058	Apart from changes in the quantity applied , no changes in topical steroids were allowed during the trial or the preceding 4 weeks .
144059	Treatment with sedative antihistamines was continued throughout the study if they were in use on entry .
144060	Assessments of disease activity
144061	The following parameters were used to monitor disease severity .
144062	Clinical severity scores — The body was divided into 10 zones : face , neck , abdomen , back , elbows , antecubital fossae , dorsa of hands , palms and wrists , popliteal fossae , and feet .
144063	Each zone was scored on a scale from 0 ( absent ) to 3 ( severe ) for : erythema , excoriation , dryness , cracking , and lichenification .
144064	Total scores from each zone were added to give a maximum of 150 .
144065	We have termed this system the ‘ Leicester score ’ .
144066	Because we had an interest in comparing methodologies , a second , simpler scoring system for clinical severity , as described by Costa et al , was also used .
144067	In this system , only the most severely affected site was assessed .
144068	Erythema , oedema , vesiculation , crusting , excoriation scaling , lichenification , pigmentation , pruritus , and sleep disturbance were each graded on a 7 point scale .
144069	This score is only briefly reported .
144070	Percentage of skin affected — This was assessed by the ‘ rule of nines ’ , as for burns injuries .
144071	Topical steroid requirement — To allow monitoring , topical steroids were prescribed by the investigator .
144072	Usage was assessed by weighing returned tubes of medication .
144073	Some patients who used potent corticosteroids also used a mild compound for the face , in which case only the potent steroid was monitored .
144074	Patient diaries — Every patient was given a diary containing a page of 10 cm visual analogue scales for baseline and each of the next 24 weeks .
144075	Scales were provided for itch , dryness , scaling , redness , and overall impression .
144076	All scales were labelled ‘ none ’ at the left-hand end and ‘ worst ever ’ at the right .
144077	Scores were added to give a maximum of 50 cm .
144078	Statistical methods
144079	We decided before starting the study that the primary response criterion would be mean change from baseline in Leicester score ( the most comprehensive single assessment ) at 16 weeks .
144080	The study was designed to have 80% power to detect a treatment response of 20% with a standard deviation ( derived from existing data ) of 30% , at significance level 0.05 .
144081	We estimated that 37 subjects would be required in each treatment limb .
144082	For each active treatment , mean changes in Leicester score between baseline and 16 weeks were compared with the placebo group by 2-tailed t tests .
144083	Results were corroborated by non-parametric tests .
144084	In addition , several secondary analyses were done .
144085	The individual components of the Leicester score , Costa scores and components , percentage of skin affected , and diary scores and components were analysed separately with t tests .
144086	As an overall test of response , improvements from baseline in Leicester scores , Costa scores , and percentage of skin affected , at all visits during treatment , were compared by repeated measures analysis of variance .
144087	We used BMDP statistical software 5V ( BMDP Statistical Software Inc , Los Angeles , USA ) for these analyses with the unstructured covariance matrix option .
144088	We also did comparisons between the placebo group and the two actively treated groups combined , and separate analyses for adults and children ( aged 12 or under ) .
144089	To investigate the effect of withdrawals , we repeated t tests at the end of treatment using the last available assessment before withdrawal of treatment .
144090	Results
144091	133 patients were enrolled .
144092	The three treatment groups were well matched at baseline for age , sex , and disease severity ( table I ) .
144093	At 4 weeks , 9 subjects had defaulted or been withdrawn , and this number increased to 14 by 8 weeks , 21 by 16 weeks , and 27 after the washout ( table II ) .
144094	4 subjects failed to attend for assessment at 4 weeks although they remained in the study .
144095	Data from the patients who withdrew were included in the analysis up to the point of withdrawal .
144096	Decisions to withdraw were made before unblinding .
144097	There were no apparent differences at baseline between the patients who withdrew and those remaining in the study .
144098	With the exception of patients withdrawn due to deterioration , there were no apparent differences in response to treatment .
144099	At 16 weeks , the mean ( SE ; number of patients ) improvements in Leicester scores were 8.48 ( 2.85 ; 33 ) for patients on epogam , 2.54 ( 2.89 ; 35 ) for patients on efamol marine , and 7.15 ( 2.88 ; 34 ) for those on placebo .
144100	On neither active regimen was mean improvement significantly different from placebo at 16 weeks ( p=0.74 for epogam , p=0.26 for efamol marine ; fig 1 ) .
144101	Mean changes at 16 weeks in individual components of the Leicester score relative to placebo are shown in fig 2 .
144102	The only significant differences were in favour of placebo over efamol marine for responses of erythema ( p=0.04 ) and cracking ( p=0.05 ) .
144103	Overall , analysis of variance for improvements in total score on each treatment at all visits showed no significant treatment effect ( p=0.17 , n=114 , 2 degrees of freedom ) .
144104	Identical analyses of Costa scores showed no significant differences , with the exception of improvement in oedema at 16 weeks in favour of epogam over placebo ( p=0.04 ) .
144105	The mean percentage of skin surface affected at 16 weeks fell 3.26% ( 4.49% ; 33 ) on epogam and 0.11% ( 4.56% ; 35 ) on efamol marine , and rose by 3.62% ( 3.52% ; 34 ) on placebo .
144106	No significant difference was found between either treatment and placebo .
144107	Complete data on topical steroid requirement were available from 26 patients on epogam , 25 on efamol marine , and 30 on placebo .
144108	Of these patients , 2 did not use any steroid , 9 were applying formulations classified in the British National Formulary as ‘ mild ’ , 17 were using ‘ moderately potent ’ compounds , 49 were using ‘ potent ’ compounds , and 4 were applying ‘ very potent ’ topical steroids .
144109	There was a reduction in steroid requirement in all three patient groups , with the largest reduction in the placebo group ( fig 3 ) .
144110	Diaries were returned by 30 patients on epogam , 35 on efamol marine , and 32 on placebo .
144111	The greatest mean overall reduction in visual analogue scales was seen in the placebo group ( fig 4 ) ; however , there were no significant differences from placebo at 16 weeks in total score or in any component .
144112	In particular , there was no significant difference in pruritus score .
144113	When analyses were repeated with both active treatment groups combined , there was no significant difference from placebo in the mean improvement of any parameter ( mean improvement in Leicester score at 16 weeks was 5.43 [ 2.05 ; 68 ] on treatment and 7.2 [ 2.88 ; 34 ] on placebo [ p=0.63 ] ) .
144114	Analysis of variance for improvements in total Leicester score at all visits again demonstrated no significant treatment effect ( p=0.98 , n=114 , 1 degree of freedom ) .
144115	Separate analyses for adults and children gave results similar to the overall analysis .
144116	Analysis with the last available assessment did not indicate any bias resulting from withdrawals .
144117	Discussion
144118	Our study has demonstrated no response of AD to EFA supplementation , nor any evidence of an additional effect when n3 series EFAs were used in combination with EFAs of the n6 series .
144119	Since both treatments consisted predominantly of evening primrose oil , we felt it reasonable to perform an analysis with the two active treatment groups combined .
144120	This analysis would be expected to provide the best chance of demonstrating a treatment effect , but no such response was found .
144121	21 ( 17% ) patients were withdrawn during treatment , presenting a potential source of bias .
144122	A perceived lack of response may have been a factor in the withdrawal of these patients , but deterioration of eczema was the principal reason for withdrawal in only 8 patients , 7 of whom were assessed at least once on treatment .
144123	Loss of data was therefore small , and analyses with the last available assessment for each subject did not indicate that any bias had been introduced .
144124	The numbers withdrawn were similar in each treatment group .
144125	It is , unlikely , therefore , that withdrawals influenced the outcome of the trial .
144126	Our results are in agreement with those of Bamford et al from the largest study yet performed on evening primrose oil in AD .
144127	These researchers recruited 154 adults and children into a placebo-controlled crossover trial and found no response to treatment .
144128	The results have been called into question because plasma lipid assays raised the possibility that placebo and active treatments had been intermixed , but Bamford et al have no reason to believe that this occurred ( personal communication ) .
144129	A similar lack of response was seen in a study of 24 subjects by Rilliet et al , in which blackcurrant seed oil was used as a source of gamma-linolenic acid .
144130	The differences between our results and those of some published studies may be partly explained by variations in design and analysis .
144131	In a crossover study of evening primrose oil and placebo in 32 adults and children with atopic eczema , each treatment was given for just 3 weeks .
144132	A significant improvement was found with active treatment but not with placebo .
144133	A more meaningful analysis — µcomparison of the mean improvement on each treatment — µcan be done from the data provided , and this analysis shows that there was no significant difference between active treatment and placebo ( t test ) .
144134	Wright and Burton performed a crossover study of evening primrose oil and placebo in 99 adults and children with atopic eczema .
144135	They reported a highly significant , dose-related response with active treatment , which reached a 43% overall improvement in patients receiving the dose used in our study .
144136	However , there are slight differences in flavour , appearance , and , possibly , laxative action between active treatment and placebo , which may have unblinded the crossover format .
144137	Furthermore , baseline comparability of treatment groups was not established .
144138	As already pointed out , it is possible that the apparent difference in response between the two groups was due to greater severity at baseline in subjects receiving active treatment .
144139	This group would then be likely to show greater spontaneous improvement .
144140	A response to evening primrose oil was also reported by Schalin-Karrila et al in a parallel-group study of 12 weeks duration with 25 adult subjects .
144141	They reported large and significant reductions ( 30–50% ) in surface area affected and severity of signs and symptoms of atopic eczema .
144142	The group on active treatment used 60% less topical steroid .
144143	However , there are clear baseline differences in disease severity between groups and the analysis did not properly address differences in response between treatments .
144144	A parallel-group study with 24 children given half the dose of evening primrose oil that we used for 4 weeks , demonstrated a significant difference between active and placebo groups , a finding that we can not explain .
144145	Three of the studies described above and five others have been the subject of a meta-analysis on the use of evening primrose oil in AD , which showed a dose-related response that increased progressively with treatment duration .
144146	A particularly consistent response was claimed for pruritus .
144147	It is important to establish baseline comparability of treatment groups in terms of disease severity in such an analysis but this issue was not addressed .
144148	We believe that the results of a meta-analysis containing unpublished trials and inadequate baseline data must be regarded with caution .
144149	Our study is the first to examine a combination of n6 series and n3 EFA supplements in AD .
144150	However , n3 series EFAs have been investigated in two smaller placebo-controlled , parallel-group trials .
144151	In the first trial , subjects ' grading of symptom severity showed a significant response , although the investigators ' assessments did not .
144152	The second trial showed no significant response .
144153	In conclusion , we believe that our study avoided the methodological and analytical problems of previous reports , which have given rise to a great deal of controversy over the efficacy of EFA supplementation in AD .
144154	No therapeutic effect was demonstrated .
144155	SHORT REPORT
144156	Epidemiology of hepatitis E virusinfection in Turkey
144157	The seroprevalence and risk factors for infection with hepatitis E virus ( HEV ) were analysed in five regions of Turkey , where one-third of acute hepatitis cases are non-A , non-B .
144158	Antibodies to HEV ( anti-HEV ) were found in 80 ( 5.9% ) of 1350 subjects .
144159	Independent predictors of anti-HEV were age over 25 years , less than elementary education , antibodies to hepatitis C virus , and residence in the warmest region ( Adana ) .
144160	Whereas none of 105 subjects in the second decade of life were HEV seropositive , 17 ( 3.7% ) of 464 and 28 ( 9.1% ) of 308 of those in the third and fourth decades of life , respectively , had anti-HEV ( p &lt; 0.001 ) .
144161	These data demonstrate that in Turkey HEV is more prevalent in warmer regions and in adults , beginning in the third decade of life .
144162	The major cause of non-parenteral non-A , non-B hepatitis has been identified and named the hepatitis E virus ( HEV ) .
144163	Serological evidence of infection with HEV ( anti-HEV ) has been found in 42% of Egyptian children with non-A , non-B hepatitis and in 71% of persons infected in a waterborne outbreak of non-A , non-B hepatitis in Kashmir , India .
144164	However , no large population-based serosurveys of HEV have been reported , and in Turkey , one-third of cases of acute hepatitis were classified as non-A , non-B .
144165	From 1990 to 1992 , demographic information and serum samples were collected for a study of cardiovascular morbidity from over 8000 persons in five distinct regions of Turkey : Istanbul , a large urban centre in the northwest ; Ayvalik , an Aegean coastal town ; Aydin , a factory city in the southwest ; Trabzon region , rural Black Sea villages in the northeast ; and Adana , a warm southeastern city , with an agricultural-based economy .
144166	All participants were volunteers responding to the advertised national heart study .
144167	Demographic information was collected by medical students administering a questionnaire .
144168	In July , 1992 , these resources were used to estimate the prevalence of HEV and hepatitis C virus ( HCV ) in Turkey .
144169	For this study , 300 persons were selected from each of the five regions with stratified random sampling based on gender , age , and income .
144170	Serum samples were placed on dry ice and stored at -70°C .
144171	Antibodies to HCV were screened with the second-generation Ortho HCV ELISA .
144172	All specimens repeatedly positive by this assay were confirmed by second-generation Chiron RIBA HCV .
144173	Antibodies to HEV were detected with Diagnostic Biotechnology 's HEV ELISA ( supplied by Genelabs Technologies ) .
144174	In this assay two recombinant antigens , which correspond to the putative structural region of the ORF3 of HEV , are coated on polystyrene microplate wells to which serum is added .
144175	These antigens correlate with the IgG and IgM response to HEV from strains as divergent as the Mexico and Burma isolates .
144176	Specimens at or above the minimum positive value were repeated in duplicate .
144177	Repeat positive specimens were considered positive .
144178	51 persons were excluded from analysis because of missing data on age , gender , or obesity , and only 201 specimens from the region of Ayvalik were tested for anti-HEV , leaving 1350 persons for subsequent analysis .
144179	Odds ratios for HEV were calculated for each covariate separately with or Fisher 's tests .
144180	Multivariate analysis was by logistic regression with anti-HEV as the dependent variable , starting with age , gender , and location as baseline covariates and with additional covariates added stepwise .
144181	Antibodies to HEV were found in 80 ( 5.9% ) of 1350 subjects .
144182	Results of univariate analysis are shown in table I.
144183	After multivariate logistic regression , only older age , lower levels of education , HCV infection , and living in Adana region were independent predictors of HEV ( table II ) .
144184	To examine further the association of age and anti-HEV , prevalence rates were calculated for each decade .
144185	Whereas none of 105 persons in the second decade of life was HEV seropositive , 17 ( 3.7% ) of 464 and 28 ( 9.1% ) of 308 of those in the third and fourth decades of life , respectively , had anti-HEV ( p &lt; 0.001 ) .
144186	The frequencies for the fifth , sixth , seventh , and eighth decades were 8/141 ( 5.7% ) , 14/161 ( 8.7% ) , 8/116 ( 6.9% ) , and 5/45 ( 11.1% ) , respectively .
144187	No clusters of HEV occurred when seropositive persons were grouped by last name or street address .
144188	Since , as with hepatitis A virus ( HAV ) , HEV is generally transmitted by faecal-oral routes , the increased prevalence of HEV in those with less education was not unexpected .
144189	Similar findings have been reported from large outbreaks where poor sanitation led to increased rates of HEV ( enteric non-A , non-B hepatitis ) in persons of lower socioeconomic strata .
144190	HEV differs from HAV in that outbreaks of HEV occur exclusively in countries with warm climates .
144191	This observation is consistent with the increased rates of HEV we observed in Adana and Aydin , warmer southern regions with similar population densities .
144192	No outbreaks of non-A , non-B hepatitis have been recognised in Adana or Aydin .
144193	HEV also differs with HAV in the increased frequency with which infection is observed in adults compared with children .
144194	Similar to the situation in developing countries , most Turkish residents are infected with HAV by the second decade of life .
144195	However , in our survey none of 105 persons in the second decade of life had anti-HEV .
144196	By contrast , we detected anti-HEV in 3.7% and 9.1% of those in the third and fourth decades of life .
144197	Although cases of HEV have been clinically and serologically documented in children , our findings are consistent with reports from several large outbreaks where high rates of HEV ( enteric non-A , non-B ) were reported in adults , beginning in the late second and third decades of life .
144198	The increased detection of anti-HEV in adults in our study could reflect a cohort of Turkish residents infected with HEV in the past and a younger generation unexposed to virus , due perhaps to improvements in sanitation .
144199	Alternatively , anti-HEV titres in subjects infected as children but not re-exposed as adults could have diminished beyond detection .
144200	EDITORIAL
144201	White elephants about town
144202	The expanding urban population in many developing countries is causing a crisis in provision of public services .
144203	Inadequate local health services for low-income groups and long queues of patients at hospitals have prompted health planners to explore the best ways of improving government health facilities .
144204	The World Health Organization , in an attempt to assist health ministries in this process , has recommended the setting up of ‘ reference centres ’ , a new tier in the health system between existing hospitals and health centres .
144205	The aim of these centres is to provide first-contact medical services 24 hours a day , obstetric services , diagnostic facilities , and inpatient care .
144206	Within their prescribed catchment area , a reference centre is responsible for the work of health centres , for community development , and for public health activities .
144207	Thus in effect reference centres are indistinguishable from small district hospitals , and they are expected to relieve the perceived overload at existing specialist city hospitals .
144208	At face value , decentralisation of services into communities seems eminently sensible , and reference centres have been effective in some countries .
144209	Some of these successful schemes are linked to universities that teach community health care and therefore need model community services to train students .
144210	The evidence that this approach will work more generally is patchy , and is furthermore based on a series of assumptions that have not been widely tested .
144211	The danger in WHO 's strong endorsement of reference centres is that governments and donors may well interpret this as a green light to invest capital in the new service tier .
144212	Much more information and research within cities is needed before the architects are called in : the research that WHO are currently coordinating in several cities in Africa and Asia must examine the assumptions underlying their policy .
144213	The WHO strategy is based on the belief that hospitals are often overloaded by patients with minor complaints who should be using cheaper and more basic services .
144214	However , there is no firm evidence that hospital overuse is a consistent feature in all countries , and this perception might well reflect overstretched hospital management in certain areas .
144215	Large patient throughput in hospitals can undoubtedly give the impression of excessive use if patients spend many hours waiting to be seen or queuing for drugs .
144216	Before making global statements about overuse , one needs to examine ward throughput and outpatient flow data against the physical and professional resources .
144217	Even if hospitals are shown to be overused , WHO policy assumes that the people using hospitals ‘ should ’ be using the health centres .
144218	An alternative view is that hospitals provide a valuable primary health service to people excluded from health centres , which focus services on mothers and children .
144219	Adolescents , men , the homeless , and people with sexually transmitted diseases may not feel comfortable in a health centre .
144220	The opening of reference centres is no guarantee of an appropriate and accessible service for these population groups .
144221	The reference centre policy also assumes that the average cost ( ie , per patient seen ) of hospital care is greater than the cost at a health centre , and that a reference centre is cheaper than a hospital .
144222	Whilst ambulatory surgical care has been shown to be cheaper than hospital care in Cali , Colombia , such evidence can not be taken as a general rule .
144223	Health centres with a low throughput may have higher average costs than a busy hospital outpatient department .
144224	A reference centre functioning as a small hospital with 24-hour cover needs many more staff than a health centre , and this will drive up recurrent costs .
144225	Unless the patient throughput per doctor or nurse at a reference centre is higher than that in the hospital , economies of scale suggest that average costs at this new tier will be greater .
144226	Few countries can afford increments in their recurrent budget .
144227	Yet this additional tier requires staff , drugs , and managerial support .
144228	Where should this come from ?
144229	With about 60–80% of government national health facility expenditure in developing countries absorbed by hospitals , an obvious source is existing hospital budgets .
144230	If planners intend to trim hospital budgets and reallocate staff to smaller facilities , this strategy must be made explicit from the outset .
144231	Although the reference centre initiative is an important stimulus for planners to evaluate their existing services , there may well be better uses for scarce resources .
144232	Capital investment is rarely a solution to complex problems , and the recurrent cost implications may be detrimental to health ministries that are already over-committed .
144233	Building a new tier in the health system is a simplistic solution to the broader problems of management and resource allocation : countries should not follow the global call blindly .
144234	COMMENTARY
144235	DRUG REACTIONS
144236	Sumatriptan and chest pain
144237	Clinical studies in over 12,000 patients have confirmed the efficacy of sumatriptan in migraine and cluster headaches .
144238	This potent and selective 5HTID receptor agonist has predominantly cranial vasoconstrictor effects in animal and human studies and can be given subcutaneously ( 6 mg ) or orally ( 100 mg ) .
144239	Sensations of heaviness , pressure , and tightness at different sites , including chest and neck , recorded in 3–5% of patients suggest some extracranial vasoactivity .
144240	During early clinical studies , 1 patient experienced cardiac ischaemic events , so a detailed safety programme was initiated ( a ) to assess the cardiovascular effects ; ( b ) to analyse reports of possible cardiac complications ; and ( c ) to conduct extensive electrocardiographic ( ECG ) monitoring during trials .
144241	Extracranial cardiovascular activity was suggested by increases in blood pressure of 12/10 mm Hg observed 10 min after subcutaneous sumatriptan and lasting for 30–60 min .
144242	A lesser effect ( 7/5 mm Hg ) of longer duration was seen with oral therapy .
144243	Detailed invasive haemodynamic investigations have now shown increased vascular resistance in both systemic and pulmonary circulations , with an increase in aortic systolic and diastolic pressures of 17–20% and 12–16% , respectively , and a relatively greater rise in pulmonary systolic and diastolic pressures of 40–50% and 33–77% .
144244	The increase in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure by 90% points to additional venoconstrictive effects .
144245	These results suggest either that 5HT receptors are more widely distributed than previously recognised or that sumatriptan is less specific in its agonist activity .
144246	In-vitro studies in human epicardial arteries confirm 5HT-like receptor activity .
144247	Maximum vasoconstriction following sumatriptan is only 21% of that seen with 5HT ( serotonin ) .
144248	The in-vivo effects were investigated in patients with chest pain but with less than critical coronary artery obstruction ( stenosis &lt;50% ) .
144249	After intravenous sumatriptan , mean absolute diameter was reduced by 14 ( SD 10 ) % vs a 16% reduction with subcutaneous administration .
144250	There was no ECG evidence of myocardial ischaemia despite symptoms of chest tingling and tightness .
144251	When serotonin was given into coronary arteries there was a 52% increase in cross-sectional area in normal arteries , a 64% reduction in patients with angina , and total occlusion in subjects with Prinzmetal angina .
144252	The reduction in cross-sectional area is at least two-fold greater than with sumatriptan .
144253	The ergot alkaloids given therapeutically in migraine have been used as a diagnostic test for coronary artery vasospasm , with a diffuse reduction in arterial diameter of about 30% evident in normal arteries .
144254	The vasoconstrictor effect is accentuated with minor arteriosclerotic disease and total occlusion may occur .
144255	In migraineurs , dihydroergotamine therapy has resulted in 18 reported cases of myocardial infarction , with death in 3. 2 patients had a history of cardiac disease .
144256	75% were less than 50 years of age , 83% were women , and 78% had no risk factors for ischaemic heart disease .
144257	Thus , the coronary vasoconstrictive effect of sumatriptan seems to be less than that of serotonin or the ergot alkaloid , which show additional 5HT and alpha-receptor stimulation .
144258	Inman and Kubota observed patients with chest tightness and suggested that asthma might be induced by sumatriptan .
144259	From the clinical database of 75 trials held by Glaxo , who manufacture sumatriptan , 375 asthmatics have been identified who had been treated for 1214 migraine episodes .
144260	Only 1 of 6 observed episodes of asthma was believed by the clinical investigators to be related to therapy .
144261	Chest tightness may indicate stimulation of pulmonary vascular receptors with pulmonary vasoconstriction rather than bronchoconstriction .
144262	Coronary vasoconstriction has been suggested by several case-reports but full cardiac investigations have seldom been carried out .
144263	Willett et al reported ST-T wave changes of Prinzmetal character 4 min after subcutaneous sumatriptan in a 47-year-old man .
144264	This patient had a history of chest pain , although a negative exercise test had been recorded 7.5 months before the episode .
144265	Underlying obstructive coronary artery disease was not excluded by angiography .
144266	Curtin et al reported ventricular fibrillation in a 42-year-old woman within 3 min of injection , thought to have been induced by vasospasm .
144267	Subsequent investigations confirmed a normal 24 h ECG recording but an exercise test suggested an ischaemic response and coronary arteriography showed a 40% obstructive lesion .
144268	This patient had experienced several episodes of palpitations although she was otherwise well .
144269	Ottervanger et al reported a myocardial infarction in a 47-year-old woman after subcutaneous sumatriptan .
144270	The ECG showed changes of inferior infarction on admission but strangely no ST elevation ; this pattern suggests a previous event or rapid spontaneous coronary artery reperfusion .
144271	She had noted chest pain after two previous injections .
144272	A subsequent exercise test showed possible ischaemic changes .
144273	Of 6124 patients with 28,648 attacks , 2150 had ECGs within 4 h of oral or subcutaneous therapy and 5388 had ECGs at some stage ( Glaxo data ) .
144274	Although 4.6% had pressure symptoms , 99% had no ECG changes .
144275	Non-specific changes were seen in 27 ( 0.5% ) ; new changes of possible myocardial ischaemia occurred in 10 ( 0.2% ) and 5 were believed to be related to sumatriptan ( 0.1% ) .
144276	The ECG change was associated with angina in only 1 case .
144277	In the subset of oral studies , ECGs were obtained in 1733 of 2786 patients with 24,000 attacks .
144278	No irreversible ECG changes were seen , although pressure symptoms occurred in 4.4% .
144279	These studies show that the frequency of ECG changes is very low .
144280	Overall , there is a small risk of myocardial ischaemia following sumatriptan-induced vasoconstriction .
144281	The drug is contraindicated in patients with symptomatic ischaemic heart disease with either angina or an earlier myocardial infarction , or if silent ischaemia or Prinzmetal angina has been documented previously .
144282	In patients who are symptom free but at risk of atheroma — eg , postmenopausal women ; men over 40 ; individuals with risk factors such as hypertension , hypercholesterolaemia , obesity , diabetes , or tobacco smoking ; and those with a strong family history — one should consider giving the first dose of sumatriptan under medical supervision .
144283	If sumatriptan induces symptoms suggestive of angina , nitrates should be given .
144284	INFECTIOUS DISEASE
144285	Antenatal interventions against sexually transmitted disease in Africa
144286	In a recent review of the effectiveness of antenatal interventions , the World Health Organization gave high priority to identifying the best ways of ensuring the availability of measures to prevent syphilis and gonorrhoea in women .
144287	The possible strategies included screening , treatment , follow-up , and health education .
144288	Such measures are required urgently in Africa , where the prevalence and complications of sexually transmitted diseases ( STDs ) remain disturbingly high .
144289	In Africa , the high overall incidence of STDs , fuelled by lack of effective STD control , means that antenatal interventions are unlikely to be very effective if they are not matched by equivalent or corresponding measures to control STDs in the general population .
144290	Moreover , the low attendance by female patients at existing STD clinics raises several questions — eg , what proportion of STDs detected antenatally represent pre-existing symptomless infection ( as a consequence of lack of partner notification ) and what proportion are acquired during pregnancy ?
144291	Successful antenatal intervention largely depends on the proportion , frequency , and pattern of attendance at antenatal clinics , so there is need for strategies to overcome cultural , demographic , and socioeconomic barriers to early and continued attendance .
144292	Nevertheless , the availability of reliable diagnostic tests and effective treatment for syphilis and gonorrhoea means that there is enormous potential and scope for reducing both their prevalence and their complications during pregnancy .
144293	There are two main options : ( a ) routine antibiotic prophylaxis ; and ( b ) case-detection through screening .
144294	Although antibiotic prophylaxis may reduce complications of some genital infections in pregnancy , the benefits are not unqualified .
144295	The data come mainly from industrialised countries where the pattern of STDs differs from that in Africa .
144296	In addition , there are obstacles to routine antibiotic prophylaxis in Africa .
144297	In view of the financial constraints , it would be hard to justify the cost of such prophylaxis for all pregnant women in order to cover 7–10% .
144298	An important consideration is that multiple drug resistance has rendered many low-cost drugs useless for this purpose .
144299	After a course of antibiotics in pregnancy , women will still be vulnerable to reinfection via sexual intercourse , while extension of prophylaxis to their spouses would double the cost without necessarily guaranteeing improved efficacy .
144300	Furthermore , blind use of antibiotics on such a large scale and the attendant difficulties with compliance might well aggravate the problem of drug resistance .
144301	Case-detection through antenatal screening may have logistic , financial , and manpower impediments to implementation but it remains the favoured strategy .
144302	The inability of many African countries to sustain large-scale routine screening for gonorrhoea with conventional methods is the main obstacle to antenatal screening for the infection .
144303	The search for cheap but reliable mass screening tests and accurate diagnostic algorithms has so far been fruitless , so case-finding based on clinical suspicion will continue to be the most important strategy .
144304	By contrast , the availability of simple , rapid , reliable , and cheap screening tests for syphilis makes this STD amenable to routine antenatal screening .
144305	A demonstration project in Zambia has shown that such screening is achievable and might significantly reduce adverse pregnancy outcomes .
144306	Mandatory antenatal screening for syphilis could be the first major antenatal intervention against STDs ; full integration of this policy into antenatal care could provide an avenue for research into pertinent questions raised in the recent WHO review and an opportunity to identify women who need evaluation for other STDs .
144307	The costs of the programme could be controlled by coordinated use of facilities and personnel in antenatal and STD clinics and laboratories .
144308	NEUROSURGERY
144309	Surgical excision for single cerebral metastasis ?
144310	In a patient with a single symptomatic metastasis in an accessible area of the brain and an otherwise reasonable outlook , the neurosurgeon may contemplate surgical excision .
144311	The usually good demarcation of tumour from normal brain allows a clean removal , quickly relieves symptoms of intracranial hypertension , and frequently improves of signs of focal brain dysfunction .
144312	Patient outcome depends largely on the extracranial disease ; the tumour seldom recurs at the site of a clean excision .
144313	Computed tomography ( CT ) with contrast enhancement facilitates the diagnosis of single lesions , but in some cases will reveal multiple metastases , which are a contraindication to surgical treatment .
144314	High-dose glucocorticoid therapy has made surgery much safer , both for tumour biopsy and for excision .
144315	Before the introduction of steroid treatment , surgical biopsy without the decompression afforded by removal of the tumour carried a prohibitive morbidity and mortality .
144316	The combination of steroids and CT-directed stereotactic brain biopsy has profoundly reduced the morbidity of the procedure : Thomas and Nouby reported mortality of 0.3% and morbidity of 4% in 300 cases , including tumours in the brainstem .
144317	Thus all solitary mass lesions in the brain can be located and verified histologically and histochemically , as they should be , before a decision on treatment .
144318	The increased safety of biopsy under steroid cover also means that one can contemplate radiotherapy as a safe treatment on its own — producing improvement in 60% of cases — rather than as an adjunct to surgical excision of the metastasis .
144319	So , what is the best treatment for the patient with a solitary cerebral metastasis — biopsy and radiotherapy , or surgical excision and radiotherapy ?
144320	The answer has not proved easy .
144321	The outcome of non-randomised studies has been influenced by the fact that the patients selected for surgery tend to be those in good overall condition with a favourable systemic prognosis .
144322	Now we have evidence from two prospective randomised studies in which surgical excision followed by radiotherapy was compared with radiotherapy alone in similar groups of steroid-treated patients with a single histologically identified brain metastasis , reasonable neurological function , and a life-expectancy greater than 6 months .
144323	In a study by Patchell et al , surgical excision and subsequent radiotherapy in 25 patients was followed by local recurrence in 5 cases vs 12 local recurrences in 23 patients treated by radiotherapy alone .
144324	Median survival was 40 weeks and functional independent survival 38 weeks in the surgical group vs 15 and 8 weeks , respectively , in the non-surgical group .
144325	Vecht et al report a randomised study of 63 patients and confirm significantly longer overall and functionally independent survival in the surgically treated patients .
144326	The results of these latest trials indicate the continuing need for close cooperation between neurosurgeons , pathologists , and radiation oncologists in the management of cancers that metastasise to the brain , not only to provide biopsy material for histological diagnosis but also to carry out excisional surgery in appropriate cases .
144327	ONCOLOGY
144328	Chromosomal deletions in haematological malignancies
144329	Haemopoiesis entails the differentiation of self-renewing pluripotential stem cells into a hierarchy of progenitor cells committed to one or more lineages .
144330	These progenitors subsequently give rise to at least nine distinct differentiated cell types .
144331	Haematological malignancies arise as a result of acquired mutations which disturb the normal balance between self-renewal and differentiation .
144332	Characterisation of these mutations might be expected to tell us something about the normal regulation of haemopoiesis .
144333	Two broad categories of tumorigenic genetic lesions are now well recognised : ( a ) activation of proto-oncogenes ; and ( b ) loss or inactivation of tumour-suppressor genes .
144334	Proto-oncogenes activated in tumours derived from a particular haemopoietic lineage are often functionally altered or ectopically expressed .
144335	Their study , although greatly increasing our understanding of tumorigenesis , has provided little information about normal haemopoietic mechanisms .
144336	By contrast , tumour-suppressor genes inactivated in tumours affecting a certain haemopoietic lineage are presumably expressed during the normal differentiation of the lineage , so their characterisation is likely to provide direct insight into the molecular mechanisms regulating such differentiation .
144337	Tumour-suppressor genes have been implicated in an increasing number of solid cancers , and some of these genes have subsequently been found to be inactivated in haematological malignancies .
144338	Thus , structural abnormalities of the retinoblastoma gene have been found in as many as 30% of some forms of leukaemia and lymphoma and mutations of the p53 gene have been reported as an infrequent event in myelodysplasia and acute myeloid leukaemia .
144339	However cytogenetic deletions at other chromosomal sites are well recognised in several haematological malignancies and are thought to flag the site of novel tumour suppressor genes .
144340	Deletions of two distinct regions of 6q have been identified in B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma but the target genes are not yet known .
144341	Deletions of 9p occur in 7–13% of patients with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia .
144342	This region of chromosome 9 contains the cluster of interferon- genes and the interferon-1 gene .
144343	Diaz et al have shown homozygous or hemizygous loss of the interferon genes in 29% of patients with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia , but it is unclear whether the critical target gene is one of the interferon genes or another locus nearby .
144344	Similarly , deletions of 13q14 in low-grade B-cell tumours may be associated with hemizygous or homozygous loss of the retinoblastoma gene .
144345	However , recent evidence suggests that the crucial event is loss of an uncharacterised neighbouring locus .
144346	Much attention has lately been focused on the 5q deletion associated with myelodysplasia and acute myeloid leukaemia .
144347	Van den Berghe and colleagues originally drew attention to the deletion of 5q in elderly female patients with macrocytic anaemia , normal or raised platelet counts , hypolobulated megakaryocytes , and a low risk of leukaemic transformation .
144348	This particular form of myelodysplasia was termed the ‘ 5q syndrome ’ .
144349	Deletions of 5q and 7q are now know to be among the commonest chromosomal abnormalities found in myelodysplasia and secondary acute myeloid leukaemia .
144350	Moreover , a whole battery of growth factors , cell surface receptors , and other tantalising genes have been mapped to the region encompassed by most 5q deletions .
144351	In 1991 , homozygous loss of the gene encoding the M-CSF receptor ( also known as FMS or CSF-1 receptor ) was shown in 4 of 10 patients with a cytogenetically detectable 5q deletion .
144352	The remaining chromosome 5 appeared normal but presumably contained a submicroscopic microdeletion in a subpopulation of cells .
144353	Could FMS itself be the target gene ?
144354	FMS is expressed in myeloid cells and FMS mutations are found in myelodysplasia .
144355	However , there have not been any reports of point mutations in the remaining FMS allele in patients with a 5q deletion .
144356	Even if FMS does not prove to be the critical target gene , characterisation of the microdeletions should considerably reduce the critical deleted region and provide a major step to identifying the real target gene .
144357	The latest twist is provided by the identification of an alternative candidate gene .
144358	The IRF-1 gene encodes a transcription factor that functions as a transcriptional activator of interferon- , interferon- , and other interferon inducible genes .
144359	Willman and co-workers looked for loss of IRF-1 and several flanking genes in 12 patients with myelodysplasia or acute myeloid leukaemia associated with cytogenetic abnormalities of 5q31 .
144360	IRF-1 was the only one of these genes consistently deleted in all of these patients .
144361	Furthermore , a rearrangement of the IRF-1 gene was identified in one additional patient with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia .
144362	These researchers suggest that IRF-1 itself could be the target gene in 5q deletions and cite two further observations as indirect support for this concept .
144363	First , interferon gene deletions have previously been associated with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and it would , therefore , not be too surprising to find that abnormalities of interferon regulation or of the interferon signalling pathway were tumorigenic .
144364	Second , in vitro experiments have shown that the balance between the transcriptional activator IRF-1 and its antagonistic repressor , IRF-2 , plays a crucial part in controlling cell growth .
144365	Overexpression of IRF-2 is tumorigenic , an effect that can be inhibited by increasing the expression of IRF-1 .
144366	These experiments provide functional evidence that IRF-1 has the potential to act as a tumour-suppressor gene .
144367	Nevertheless , direct evidence implicating IRF-1 as the critical target gene in 5q deletions remains sparse .
144368	The only structural abnormality of IRF-1 was found in a patient with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia , a disease not normally associated with 5q deletions .
144369	The significance of this rearrangement for the pathogenesis of myeloid malignancies associated with 5q deletions remains unclear .
144370	These results raise several questions .
144371	Perhaps the most important is whether the FMS and IRF-1 data can be reconciled .
144372	FMS and IRF-1 are separated by an estimated 5–12 megabases and microdeletions that include one are unlikely to include the other .
144373	One possible explanation would be the existence of two distinct target genes on 5q , one in the region of IRF-1 and the other close to FMS .
144374	This speculation would accord with the fact that some patients with myelodysplasia and a 5q deletion have a very low risk of transformation ( eg , 5q syndrome ) whereas in other myelodysplasia patients a 5q deletion is associated with poor prognosis ( eg , secondary MDS ) .
144375	These examples illustrate the central problem of characterising chromosomal deletions — how do you know when you have identified the target gene ?
144376	Searching for mutations in a candidate gene probably remains the best approach , albeit a labour-intensive one .
144377	However , once identified , the target genes should be doubly interesting since they promise to shed light not only on the pathogenesis of haematological malignancies but also on the normal regulation of haemopoietic differentiation .
144378	CLINICAL PRACTICE
144379	Irritable bowel syndrome : pathogenesis and management
144380	An international working team defined the irritable bowel syndrome as distinct from other functional bowel disorders .
144381	Symptom criteria for the irritable bowel syndrome are known as the Rome criteria .
144382	Since there is no pathophysiological marker for any of these syndromes we must rely on symptoms for their definition and classification .
144383	The Rome nosology is a step towards better understanding of functional gastrointestinal disorders because the disparate syndromes are likely to have different causes and treatments .
144384	Epidemiology
144385	Studies in the UK , USA , France , New Zealand , and China indicate that irritable bowel syndrome ( IBS ) is present in 11–14% of adults .
144386	Although most people with IBS in the community do not consult a physician for their symptoms ; the treatment of those who do is time-consuming and expensive .
144387	Management strategy must be developed with this in mind .
144388	Pathogenesis
144389	Is the IBS ‘ … a qualitative , or merely quantitative departure from the psychophysiologic reactions of normal people ? ’ — Thomas Almy , 1980
144390	The cause of IBS has confounded physicians for almost two centuries .
144391	Despite much research we can not even today offer a convincing explanation .
144392	Some declare it is caused by diet ; others are convinced it is a motility disorder or due to altered perception , a psychological disorder , a psychophysiological phenomenon , or even abnormal illness behaviour .
144393	Keeping Professor Almy 's question in mind , a condition affecting at least 11% of a physically healthy population may be no disease at all .
144394	A dietary disorder ?
144395	‘ Eat what you want and let the food fight it out inside ’ — Mark Twain
144396	Dennis Burkitt in East Africa noted that constipation and other ‘ western ’ bowel disorders were uncommon in natives consuming an indigenous high-fibre diet .
144397	In 1972 a study of rural African and westernised populations noted that the greater the dietary fibre content , the greater the daily stool weight and the shorter the whole-gut transit time .
144398	These observations led to the ‘ fibre hypothesis ’ : the concept that many diseases of the colon and other organs , including IBS , result from the ingestion of a western , refined , low-fibre diet .
144399	Subsequent studies confirmed that a high-fibre diet increases stool bulk and shortens gut transit .
144400	The value of bran , psyllium , and other bulking materials is well established in the treatment of constipation .
144401	The presence of IBS in individuals has not been linked to their fibre intake and its presence in countries such as China makes it unlikely that a single dietary factor such as fibre deficiency is at fault .
144402	Dietary fibre supplements have not been successful in the treatment of IBS as measured by double-blind trials , although there is evidence that at least 30 g of dietary fibre a day will improve constipation and some other symptoms .
144403	The fibre story is even more confused by the report that , among ‘ healthy ’ volunteers , an outgoing personality and positive self-image are associated with a larger stool output .
144404	Some patients have no doubt that a food is the culprit .
144405	This idea has spawned irrational diets that defy science , cause much inconvenience , and may even threaten nutrition .
144406	True food allergy , such as to shellfish , affects systems beyond the gut and is more likely to cause vomiting and diarrhoea than IBS symptoms .
144407	Certain non-IgE-mediated intolerances to wheat , dairy products , or beef are claimed to cause diarrhoea but not IBS as strictly defined .
144408	Few patients with IBS can be confirmed by double-blind feedings to have a true food sensitivity .
144409	Nevertheless , evidence for lactose intolerance , excessive caffeine intake , use of sorbitol-containing gum , or other drug or dietary habit that might affect the gut should be sought .
144410	A motility disorder ?
144411	‘ The bowels are at one time constipated , at another lax , in the same person …
144412	How the disease has two such different symptoms I do not profess to explain … ’ — W. Cumming , London Medical Gazette , 1849 .
144413	Despite the evident gut malfunction in IBS the pathophysiology is obscure .
144414	Colon motility studies in the 1960s suggested that in constipation , the motility index ( frequency×amplitude of contraction ) is increased , holding up passage of stool and causing abdominal pain .
144415	Conversely , the motility index is decreased in those with diarrhoea , so that the sigmoid behaves like a sphincter .
144416	The index has not proved to be a reliable feature of either constipation or diarrhoea .
144417	The proximal colon and the small intestine are also thought to be dysfunctional in IBS .
144418	In the 1970s , investigators reported that a 3 cycle/min colonic myoelectrical rhythm is commoner in IBS patients than in controls , although the specificity of this observation is now doubted .
144419	European workers associated the recording of electrical short bursts in the colon with constipation and their absence with diarrhoea .
144420	In the 1980s attention was drawn to the small bowel , where the secretory and motor responses to stress seem to be different in IBS patients .
144421	None of these phenomena is sufficiently specific to permit its use as a diagnostic test of IBS nor do any of them offer an explanation of how symptoms are generated .
144422	In a series of experiments , balloons inflated sequentially throughout the gut identified trigger points that reproduced the abdominal pain in most cases of IBS .
144423	Even here we can not be sure to what extent the pain of IBS is a normal perception of abnormal physiology or a normal perception of normal phenomena .
144424	In IBS there is a tendency for both small and large bowel to over-react to various stimuli such as drugs , stress , balloon distension , and even eating , which may represent an exaggerated gastrocolonic response .
144425	A perception disorder ?
144426	‘ … a normal perception of abnormal motility or an abnormal perception of normal motility … ’ — M. J. Ford , 1986 .
144427	The failure of motility observations adequately to explain symptoms has led many to consider the sensory or afferent connections between the gut and the brain .
144428	It has been shown , for example , that IBS patients experience pain at lower volumes of rectal distension than others .
144429	The autonomic connections between the enteric and central nervous systems are well known , and the vagus and sympathetic nerves carry more afferent than efferent nerve fibres .
144430	The experience of pain may be greatly influenced by emotion , memory , culture , and the psychosocial situation .
144431	It is useful to distinguish acute from chronic pain .
144432	The former is linked to tissue disease or organ dysfunction , and in the case of the gut is associated with eating , defaecation , and vomiting .
144433	Chronic pain is continuous and unassociated with the physiological responses to acute pain such as sweating and tachycardia .
144434	The patient with chronic pain is often mentally depressed and there may have been adverse experiences such as sexual abuse or threatening life events .
144435	Acute , function-related pain is primarily sensory or peripheral , and may lend itself to treatment with analgesics directed to the involved organ .
144436	Chronic pain , which is more influenced by central controlling activity , may require a different approach .
144437	Thus , drugs such as tricyclic antidepressants enhance serotonin release and inhibit pain impulses , thereby closing the ‘ gate ’ on the perception of noxious stimuli .
144438	They may also enhance endorphin release .
144439	The use of benzodiazepines risks habituation and , via gamma-aminobutyric acid production , these drugs may inhibit serotonin and further open the ‘ gate ’ .
144440	Not only pain may be misperceived .
144441	Patients often misinterpret their bowel action as well .
144442	Although stool frequency in the population ranges from 3/week to 3/day , variations within this range may be considered abnormal , and frequent but fragmented or lumpy stool as diarrhoea .
144443	There is no evidence that the occurrence of borborygmi , flatus , and distension differ from those in other people .
144444	Lasser and Levitt found that patients complaining of ‘ gas ’ or ‘ bloating ’ had no excess intestinal gas .
144445	Altered perception alone does not explain IBS .
144446	It does not explain the triggering sensation and altered function of the gut , nor does it seem important in those with IBS symptoms who do not seek medical care .
144447	A psychological disorder ?
144448	The notion that the IBS is related to or even caused by the patient 's psychological state is as old as the concept of IBS itself .
144449	Many studies attest to the fact that anxiety , mental depression , and other types of psychological distress are more likely in IBS patients than in those with organic disease .
144450	Such studies are of patients in a tertiary care setting who are unlikely to be representative of all persons experiencing IBS symptoms .
144451	Whitehead found that the psychosocial make-up of patients with IBS in the community who do not see doctors is the same as that of normal people .
144452	There are no studies of the psychological state of IBS patients seen in primary care , but it is reasonable to assume that they represent an intermediate population .
144453	In one British clinic , chronic attenders with IBS were compared with newly referred patients .
144454	Although psychological morbidity was similar in the two groups , the social consequences in the chronic attenders were more severe .
144455	The foregoing data do not support the notion that psychopathology causes IBS .
144456	Perhaps psychopathology elevates IBS symptoms to the status of a medical problem in a person 's consciousness ?
144457	For the emotionally troubled person , IBS symptoms may provide a socially acceptable vehicle for care .
144458	This argument is reinforced by observations that IBS patients consult more often than others after a stressful or threatening life event .
144459	A person with IBS who has ignored the symptoms for years may become acutely aware of them when a close relative succumbs to cancer .
144460	Treatment here is obvious .
144461	Management of patients whose visits seem to be precipitated by depression , job loss , marriage break up , or other personal catastrophe may be much more complex .
144462	Many tertiary care patients have sustained sexual or physical abuse .
144463	In such a situation undue focus on the gut symptoms may be misplaced .
144464	A psychophysiological disorder ?
144465	We all recognise that emotion affects gut function .
144466	Who has not experienced some gut upset before an exam , a marriage , or other stressful emotional event ? 40 years ago Almy showed that stress could alter gut function but that these changes were not specific to the stress .
144467	One person may have ‘ butterflies ’ , another diarrhoea , another vomiting , and yet another a migraine .
144468	In IBS the relation of symptoms to stress is more subtle .
144469	Some notice that symptoms improve during a crisis , only to return later .
144470	In patients with IBS the gut seems to be more reactive to various stimuli when compared with controls .
144471	Drugs , hormones , food , distension , and emotional stress elicit exaggerated motor responses .
144472	Using radiotelemetry equipment , Valori et al observed that motility of the small bowel was altered in a different manner in patients with IBS than in controls .
144473	He and his colleagues employed such stressors as heavy-metal music , nocturnal arousal , or parking in London traffic to challenge the small bowel .
144474	Are the above observations clues to the cause of IBS or merely epiphenomena ?
144475	A behavioural disorder ?
144476	A random telephone survey in Cincinnati compared people with peptic ulcer with those with IBS .
144477	The latter had more somatic symptoms , viewed colds and influenza more seriously , and consulted physicians more frequently for minor complaints .
144478	During childhood they also were more likely that others to have received gifts or remained home from school when ill .
144479	This report concludes that people with IBS are prone to chronic illness behaviour and that this is learned .
144480	The notion is gaining credence that health-care seeking in IBS , particularly to tertiary care centres , may have as much to do with a person 's cultural and psychosocial state as with the IBS symptoms themselves .
144481	How else can one explain why women are more likely than men to take their IBS symptoms to a doctor in western cultures , whereas the opposite is true in India ?
144482	Why do only a minority of those with IBS seek medical attention ?
144483	The concurrence of threatening life events and psychosocial distress may partly explain these phenomena .
144484	Therapeutic approach
144485	We must develop a strategy of management based upon the known facts .
144486	Such a strategy should be based on 5 principles : a positive diagnosis , consideration of the patient 's agenda , critical appraisal of drugs and placebos , continuing care , and a graded therapeutic response .
144487	Positive diagnosis
144488	‘ … one who has seen many such cases can with tolerable certainty tell , without more minute examination what the nature of the complaint is. ’ — W. Cumming , London Medical Gazette , 1849 .
144489	Longitudinal studies indicate that the condition affects people over long periods of their lives yet there is no evidence that they are at risk of any serious organic disease .
144490	Furthermore , a careful history and physical examination permit a confident diagnosis that stands up over time .
144491	Because some physicians regard IBS as a diagnosis of exclusion they feel compelled to exclude all organic disease .
144492	This approach is expensive .
144493	The physician should attempt to establish a positive diagnosis at the first clinical encounter , based on the criteria in table II .
144494	In a condition that affects up to 14% of the population , organic disease is bound to coexist in some .
144495	The first step is to inquire after symptoms that suggest organic disease such as anaemia , bleeding , fever , weight-loss or a recent change in bowel habit .
144496	If such symptoms and physical findings are absent , few investigations should be undertaken .
144497	A sigmoidoscopy should be done but biopsy in search of microscopic colitis in the absence of continuous diarrhoea is unnecessary .
144498	If the patient is over 40 or has risk factors for colon carcinoma , a barium enema is prudent .
144499	Other tests should be avoided unless indicated .
144500	An early , confident diagnosis permits tests to be kept to a minimum and reassures the patient that there is no mortal disease .
144501	Such reassurance may be the physician 's most effective therapeutic weapon .
144502	Patient 's agenda
144503	We have seen that most people with IBS do not consult doctors and those who do may have reasons other than the symptoms themselves .
144504	Severity of symptoms may be important but psychosocial factors must also affect the decision .
144505	The answer to the question ‘ Why has this patient come to see the doctor now ? ’ may be a good therapeutic clue .
144506	Fear of serious disease should be met with firm reassurance that none exists .
144507	Threatening life events should be discussed .
144508	Some patients may require psychological help or stress management skills , but simple supportive psychotherapy by the attending physician can be salutary .
144509	In a Swedish study , patients with IBS treated with eight sessions of ‘ supportive psychotherapy which could be performed in any physician 's office ’ had fewer symptoms and psychological and physical disability compared with a control group when they were seen 3 months later .
144510	This observation supports the notion that early , careful attention to the patient 's psychosocial concerns is effective and has lasting benefit .
144511	Such an approach is validated by a UK study which also showed that improvement is most likely if psychopathology is recognised and the pain is not constant .
144512	Anxiety and depression must be treated on their own merits .
144513	Although psychotherapeutic agents do not alter IBS symptoms , treatment of the psychological distress may help a patient to cope with them .
144514	In some pain-dominant patients with IBS , tricyclic antidepressants may be helpful even if depression is not obvious .
144515	These drugs have proved effective in other chronic pain syndromes .
144516	They may act via central pathways that influence the perception of pain .
144517	Drugs and placebos
144518	‘ … not a single study offers convincing evidence that any therapeutic agent is effective in treating the IBS symptom complex . ’
144519	— D. B. Klein , 1988 .
144520	Klein reviewed the so-called controlled trials of drugs in IBS over 20 years and found them all flawed .
144521	The entry criteria were usually unclear , and the symptom criteria of Manning , Kruis , and Rome are recent innovations .
144522	Many studies were too small , too short , or had too many drop-outs .
144523	Others had inappropriate trial design or were marred by faulty statistical analysis .
144524	No drug has been proven globally effective in IBS .
