145092	Convergent combination chemotherapy refers to the use of several antiretroviral drugs — nucleoside and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase ( RT ) inhibitors — to damage the virus to such a degree that its replication is permanently impaired .
145093	The efficacy of this approach with zidovudine , didanosine , and nevirapine has been reported in vitro and was further discussed in Berlin .
145094	Over 400 patients have already been recruited into a trial to test this regimen .
145095	Intriguing in-vitro studies also suggest that introduction of resistance mutations to one antiretroviral compound ( didanosine ) can diminish previously documented resistance to another agent ( zidovudine ) .
145096	However , Robert Gallo voiced concern about multidrug cocktails .
145097	The more drugs that one gives , the more likely it is that damage to host DNA polymerase will take place .
145098	The potential toxicity of these agents should not be underestimated .
145099	Much emphasis has been placed on the theoretical value of tat and protease inhibitors .
145100	The tat ( transactivator ) gene of HIV controls the rate of viral DNA replication .
145101	In vitro , Ro-24-7429 , a benzodiazepine derivative , inhibits RNA replication and viral protein production .
145102	In a randomised blinded phase I/II trial comparing Ro-24-7429 with nucleoside RT inhibitors in 96 patients ( CD4 50–500/L ) , Haubrich et al ( California , USA ) found that although the drug was well tolerated , it was ineffective in producing either a rise in CD4 count or a fall in p24 antigen activity .
145103	Inhibition of HIV protease should slow maturation of virion core proteins and retroviral enzymes .
145104	Nanomolar concentrations of protease inhibitors show highly specific antiretroviral activity .
145105	An Abbot protease inhibitor ( A77003 ) given intravenously produced no beneficial changes in CD4 count or p24 antigen in 22 HIV-positive patients ( mean CD4 300/L ) .
145106	In a few cases , there was a decline in quantitative HIV culture from plasma ( but not from peripheral blood mononuclear cells ) .
145107	Roche 's oral protease inhibitor , Ro-31-8959 , was tested in three phase I/II protocols : advanced disease with ( France ) and without ( Italy ) previous zidovudine treatment , and symptom-free or minimally symptomatic disease ( UK ) .
145108	Although well tolerated , the effects on CD4 count , p24 antigen , and HIV titres from mononuclear cells and plasma were weak and variable .
145109	In the Italian study , the effects of Ro-31-8959 were comparable with zidovudine .
145110	Clinical trials of antisense oligonucleotides that bind to and inhibit the HIV gag gene sequence will begin later this year with GEM 91 ( genetic expression modulation ) from Hybridon .
145111	For the future , the application of dominant negative viral mutants ( which , when mixed with wild-type virus , render it non-infectious ) , capsid-targeted virus inactivation ( a similar process leading to viral degradation rather than inactivation ) , and virus-specific inhibition ( for instance , by targeting the rev response element that is essential for normal rev protein function in virus assembly ) was discussed by Max Essex ( Harvard AIDS Institute , USA ) and F. Wong-Staal ( California , USA ) .
145112	Where are the glimmers of hope ?
145113	Despite Anthony Fauci 's assertion that ‘ the virus is the major factor in HIV disease , ’ it was clear that a shift in emphasis is taking place from direct antiretroviral strategies to immune-directed therapies .
145114	HIV infection induces a state of immune activation leading to loss of follicular dendritic cells and normal lymph node architecture .
145115	Interference with this process by targeting the activated T cell , apoptosis , or cytokine secretion might stabilise the immune system and control the course of infection .
145116	Effective cell-mediated immunity is central to limiting viral damage .
145117	Gallo noted that virus replicated faster in an activated cell where deoxyribonucleotides are in plentiful supply .
145118	Hydroxyurea inhibits the rate-limiting enzyme supplying deoxyribonucleotides — ribonucleotide reductase — and substantially diminishes HIV replication .
145119	Gallo also quoted some of the latest work of Daniel Zagury 's team which has discovered a pentapeptide motif in gp120 which is also present in CD4 and which interferes with antigen activation possibly leading to a state of cell anergy and immunodeficiency .
145120	The case for autoimmune damage in HIV infection was supported by Wilson et al ( London , UK ) who have found a 13 aminoacid sequence in gp120 that mimics human MHC molecules .
145121	If autoimmune processes are important , T cell vaccination might be a suitable treatment strategy .
145122	Jonas Salk 's team in California , USA , reported the first results of phase I/II clinical trials with a gp 120-depleted treatment vaccine .
145123	Both humoral and cell-mediated immune responses were generated and HIV copy number fell during the vaccination period compared with controls .
145124	The promise of immunotherapeutic strategies to combat HIV infection was one strong and clear message to emerge from Berlin .
145125	The next world AIDS conference will take place in Yokohama , Japan , in 1994 and subsequent meetings will be held biennially .
145126	Medicine and the Law
145127	Triazolam licensing in UK
145128	Acting on the advice of the Committee on Safety of Medicines ( CSM ) , the UK Department of Health suspended the product licences for triazolam ( Halcion ) on Sept 30 , 1991 .
145129	On June 12 , 1993 , despite a hard-fought battle by the manufacturers , Upjohn Ltd — who have now exhausted all the statutory avenues of appeal provided by the Medicines Act 1968 — the Licensing Authority announced that the revocation of licences would be permanent .
145130	Upjohn appealed to the CSM but its application was unsuccessful .
145131	In May , 1992 , the company took its case to the Medicines Commission , which advised revocation of licences for 0.25 mg products but thought that problems with 0.125 mg tablets could be dealt with otherwise .
145132	The Licensing Authority , however , proposed on July 17 , 1992 , that licences for both dosages be revoked .
145133	Since that determination went against advice from the Medicines Commission , Upjohn invoked the right , rarely exercised , to present its case to a panel appointed by the Licensing Authority under the 1968 Act .
145134	The four-day hearing was in private but the panel 's 37-page report is in the public domain .
145135	Its findings were sympathetic to Upjohn 's case — ie , ‘ the data are generally reassuring but rare idiosyncratic episodes of violence in association with triazolam , as with other [ benzodiazepines ] , can not be ruled out ’ .
145136	Notwithstanding the best efforts of the distinguished panel , the findings were arrived at after a one-sided presentation of evidence and argument .
145137	Furthermore , much of the evidence can not be independently assessed .
145138	For instance , the finding on equivalent doses ( which is at odds with the views of the CSM ) is handled by reference to oral evidence , to published work , and to a transcript .
145139	No attempt is made to summarise or to quote extensively or to append the reference documents .
145140	As the panel notes , the statutory procedure makes no provision for a balanced argument ; only Upjohn was able to present its case and its witnesses and evidence , though the Licensing Authority provided material and the panel ‘ followed up leads from this material and from that presented by Upjohn ’ .
145141	The panel notes that ‘ it would be simpler and much more satisfactory if the procedure provided for the ‘ contrary case ’ to be presented'' .
145142	The panel is clearly dissatisified with its remit ‘ only to hear the licence holder ’ and , after an extensive examination of the evidence , to report to , but not be entitled to make recommendations to , the Licensing Authority .
145143	The panel concludes that overall the benefits outweighed the risks of the drug at doses of 0.25 and 0.125 mg when provided with appropriate data sheets .
145144	One ‘ vital area ’ was that of ‘ equivalent dose ’ .
145145	The panel notes difficulty in making exact comparisons but found the weight of evidence was ‘ in favour of a dose of 0.25 mg triazolam being roughly equivalent to a dose of 30 mg flurazepam or 20 mg temazepam ( UK formulation ) .
145146	We accept this represents a major change from earlier views that the equivalent doses were triazolam 0.5 mg to 30 mg flurazepam or 20 mg temazepam ’ .
145147	The Licensing Authority is unconvinced by this finding which is , in effect , that the triazolam doses in comparative trials were not equivalent to those of flurazepam .
145148	Protocol 321 ( in prison volunteers ) was of ‘ marginal value ’ in assessing the safety of the drug in 1993 , the panel felt , and Upjohn 's explanation that the incomplete information on adverse effects was due to a transcribing error , is ‘ not implausible , although … even in 1978 , a properly organised company should have operated checks which eliminated such errors ’ .
145149	One difficulty those advising the Licensing Authority had to contend with was the ‘ relative lack of data about the efficacy and effects of triazolam at the licensed doses of 0.125 mg and 0.25 mg ’ and at the beginning of the hearing that problem troubled the panel also .
145150	‘ … we find it unfortunate that Upjohn failed to respond at all readily to requests made by the Licensing Authority as early as 1990 , that they should carry out a new post-marketing surveillance study ’ .
145151	However , the panel was impressed ( more so than the Minister ) with a UK post-marketing surveillance study .
145152	The panel felt that the starting dose for triazolam in the young and middle-aged ought to be 0.125 mg , increasing to 0.250 mg ‘ only if necessary ’ .
145153	The same logic suggests that the elderly should be started on 0.0625 mg , but no data are yet available ( a US study is expected to be available this year ) .
145154	Shortly before the publication of this report saw the successful appeal against the Legal Aid Board 's refusal to allow potential Halcion claims to be investigated where applications for legal aid were made after the deadline of Oct 20 , 1991 .
145155	This date was imposed by Mr Justice Kennedy , limiting the right of entry by legally aided litigants into the first group action in the multiplaintiff benzodiazepine litigation .
145156	Some 580 claimants , many of whom came forward after the critical BBC Panorama television programme on triazolam in October , 1991 , can expect to receive limited legal aid to allow for investigation of their claims .
145157	The audit of Halcion claims along with some 3000 Ativan ( lorazepam ) claims already served , is due to be completed shortly .
145158	Further judicial directions in the proceedings of the litigation are expected in July .
145159	Upjohn has at all times contended that Halcion is safe and effective and that any errors in the presentation of its material to the Licensing Authority were unintended , and it is suing the BBC for libel .
145160	The company is also suing Prof Ian Oswald , a psychiatrist expert in the field of sleep and hypnotics , and he is counterclaiming for libel .
145161	The cases are due to be heard together before a judge in London without a jury , in January .
145162	Noticeboard
145163	1992–97 AIDS projections for England and Wales
145164	Revised calculations from a working group chaired by Prof N. E. Day suggest that there will be between 1945 and 3215 new AIDS cases in 1997 .
145165	Projected annual incidences for 1997 in each of the main exposure categories are : homosexual males , 1350 ; injecting drug users , 165 ; and heterosexuals , 770 .
145166	Day and colleagues estimated that there were about 23,400 HIV-infected individuals in England and Wales by the end of 1991 .
145167	Although a plateau will develop in the overall incidence of AIDS , there are strikingly different predictions for each exposure category .
145168	For homesexual males , the annual incidence of AIDS is expected to plateau in 1994 in line with a peak annual incidence of HIV infection in 1983–84 .
145169	Among injecting drug users , the peak in HIV incidence took place in 1985 and so the number of AIDS cases is still climbing .
145170	For heterosexuals up to 1991 , the peak of HIV infection had yet to be reached and so one can expect a continued rise in the annual incidence of AIDS cases for some time to come .
145171	The pool of those with HIV infection acquired heterosexually via a partner who had also been infected heterosexually is slowly increasing .
145172	The UK Department of Health claims that its AIDS prevention policy is responsible both for the reduction in projected new cases among injecting drug users and the greater certainty about heterosexual exposure .
145173	According to Baroness Cumberlege , ‘ the UK now has one of the lowest estimated HIV prevalence rates in western Europe ’ .
145174	Day attributes the changes to more detailed and reliable data collection , together with better statistical techniques .
145175	The report adopts a cautious note , reflecting concern about a possible recent increase in HIV transmission among homosexual males and the difficulty of guessing sexual mixing patterns between subsets of the population .
145176	The latest figures replace 1990 estimates that have proved to be reasonably accurate except for an overestimate of the number of heterosexual exposures ( 355 vs 255 ) and an underestimate of cases among homosexual males ( 910 vs 1165 ) .
145177	Gases and glues
145178	Data on deaths in the UK from volatile substances abuse ( VSA ) have been recorded by a team from the Department of Public Health Sciences , St George 's Hospital Medical School , London , since 1971 , and these data have been collected in a ‘ stable and systematic ’ manner since 1983 .
145179	The latest report from St George 's , which covers the period up to the end of 1991 , shows that there were 122 deaths from VSA in 1991 compared with 151 in 1990 and 113 in 1989 .
145180	Since 1983 , there has been an average annual increase in VSA deaths of 5.4% per annum .
145181	Young people aged 14–18 years are the age group most likely to die from VSA , accounting for 61.5% of all VSA deaths between 1971 and 1991 , and the figures for 1991 show no significant change in this pattern .
145182	87% of deaths from VSA in 1991 were in males , and again this percentage did not differ from the overall figure since 1971 .
145183	Between 1971 and 1991 , the most popular substances for abuse were gas fuels ( primarily cigarette-lighter refills and bottled domestic gases ; 35.1% of deaths ) , aerosols ( primarily deodorants/antiperspirants and pain-relief sprays ; 20.9% ) , glues ( mostly contact adhesives ; 19.2% ) , and ‘ other ’ ( typewriter correction fluid and anaesthetic gases figure prominently in this group , which also included petrol , plastic remover , and dry-cleaning fluid ; 20.7% ) .
145184	With the exception of glue ( 13.9% ) , the figures for substances abused in 1991 differ little from the overall figures .
145185	In 1991 , VSA was most likely to occur in a public place ( 42% ) or at home ( 39% ) .
145186	Unsurprisingly , most deaths from VSA were in hospital or on the way to hospital ( 47% ) , and causes of death were recorded as direct toxic effects ( 49.2% ) , inhalation of vomit ( 14.8% ) , trauma — eg , hanging or drowning ( 11.5% ) , suffocation inside a plastic bag ( 7.4% ) , and ‘ other/not known ’ ( 17.2% ) .
145187	From February , 1992 , the UK Department of Health sponsored the broadcast of television commercials designed to alert parents to the dangers of VSA .
145188	The next report on VSA deaths should reveal what effect , if any , this campaign has had .
145189	Financing health service
145190	Until recently , most national governments muddled along with health-care systems derived from a mixture of charitable support , private practice , and voluntary or compulsory insurance .
145191	Health care was seldom a major political issue , and inequalities in its provision were considered as inevitable as inequalities in wealth .
145192	WHO turns its attention to the matter in its latest Technical Report , which notes the experience of representative nations from Algeria to Zimbabwe .
145193	Just how diverse they are is shown by the proportion of health care provided privately .
145194	Among the richer nations , in the USA 58% of health care is private , and in the UK , 13% .
145195	In developing nations , the extremes are 80% in Uganda and 12% in Lesotho .
145196	Within such diversity there is no common standard of achievable health care .
145197	WHO suggests there should be , and , if not a common way of paying for it , at least an agreed means of approaching the difficulties involved .
145198	In the UK , the tide is turning from all-out provision of health care by central government to a hybrid where private initiatives are encouraged to compete within state funding .
145199	A more radical change may be on the way : a report by the UK Institute of Health Services Management concludes that ‘ General taxation must be reconsidered as the major funding of the National Health Service if it continues to fail to deliver adequate levels of resources ’ .
145200	Coincidentally , the UK Government 's Department of Health launches a ‘ Help us to help you ’ campaign , wherein sick people are advised how not to waste the limited funds available for their treatment ( ‘ … remember to cancel appointments if they can not be kept … ’ ) and reminded by the Secretary of State for Health that ‘ Our primary care system is also the source of considerable envy abroad ’ , as I was reminded again during a recent trip to Russia .
145201	Russia 's envy is understandable when , under communist government , the state 's doctors were so slightly rewarded as to make illegal private practice inevitable .
145202	Whether Russia 's change to a market economy will lead to the concept of free health care being abandoned , remains to be seen .
145203	In the UK , this ideal has been eroding for some time and seems unlikely to survive the escalating costs of current treatments .
145204	WHO and Yugoslavia
145205	Dr Nils Rosdahl , former director of public health in Denmark , has taken up a WHO assignment as adviser to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees in former Yugoslavia .
145206	Based in Zagreb , he succeeds Sir Donald Acheson , who went there in July last year on what was expected to be a two or three month assignment .
145207	WHO now has some fifty staff in the area , half of whom are locally engaged .
145208	On return from a ten-day visit to the five republics of former Yugoslavia , Dr Hiroshi Nakajima , WHO Director-General , was visibly appalled by what he had seen in Bosnia-Herzegovina particularly the destruction of some 260 hospitals and the gravity of the wounds caused by the high-velocity bullets .
145209	Some children among Sarajevo 's 330,000 inhabitants were showing signs of malnutrition .
145210	Diarrhoea and dysentery outbreaks were increasing and tuberculosis and hepatitis were major threats .
145211	State dispensaries no longer had even the most common antibiotics .
145212	Dr Nakajima , accompanied on his tour by Dr Jo Asvall , head of WHO 's European regional office in Copenhagen , said that he had been asked several times if Yugoslav funds frozen in the US and other countries could not be used for purchase of medical supplies .
145213	He promised to pass this idea on .
145214	Harmonising therapeutics teaching in Europe
145215	The European Network of Therapeutics Teachers ( ENOTT ) has been formed to encourage the optimisation and harmonisation of undergraduate and postgraduate therapeutics teaching in Europe .
145216	Some of their aims are that learning methods should be non-directive , interactive , and based on clinical cases and that teaching should foster the ability to evaluate critically published data on different treatments and new drugs .
145217	They also believe that therapeutics should be examined as a separate subject in the final year of undergraduate study and that emphasis should be given to therapeutics throughout the whole medical curriculum , with a minimum of 100 hours being dedicated specifically to the subject .
145218	Further information can be had from Prof A. Benetos , Hospital Broussais , Service de Medicine 1 , 96 rue Didot , 75674 Paris Cedex 14 , France .
145219	Life expectancy and handedness
145220	R. Peel , left arm slow with 102 test wickets against Australia , died aged 84 after an irregular , even accident-prone , life .
145221	Not a classic illustration of the thesis of Aggleton and colleagues , who have been looking at the lifespans of cricketers and report a two-year gap in favour of right-handers , much of it ascribable to fewer deaths in accidents or in war .
145222	Yorkshire cricket has been graced with world-class slow bowlers .
145223	Rhodes , like Peel , lived to a great age ; others did not ; and one was killed in action .
145224	But this study , from psychologists in Durham , is demography not anecdote .
145225	Their source is Who 's Who of Cricketers ( 1984 ) in which Aggleton et al found 3165 dead ones whose handedness could be determined .
145226	This game is one where left-handedness has some advantage and considerable nuisance value so it is not surprising that as many as 18.5% of these first-class performers were left-handed .
145227	The focus of the paper is the 147 cricketers known to have died from unnatural causes ( excluding suicide ) .
145228	28.6% were left-handed and this figure was much the same for those killed in action and for those killed in other ways .
145229	With earlier hints from baseball these data point to an ergonomic cause — ie , machinery and systems designated by the right-handed for right-handers — rather than more elaborate explanations , such as the immunological .
145230	NHS staff and the media
145231	The National Health Service has issued its guidelines to staff on their right to speak out on concerns about health care ( NHS executive letter EL[93]51 ) .
145232	Unauthorised disclosure to the media is no longer described as a ‘ potentially serious breach of contract ’ ( see Lancet Oct 24 , 1992 , p 1031 , and Nov 21 , p 1277 for draft guidance ) , but the new advice says that if such disclosure is judged to be unjustified it could result in disciplinary action .
145233	Pharmacovigilance in Europe
145234	A European Pharmacovigilance Research Group ( EPRG ) has been set up ; it was established with support from the European Commission under the Biomed Programme to develop and validate methods of pharmacovigilance that are applicable to the divergent patterns of health care delivery across the European Community and that are compatible with national legal , cultural , and ethical customs .
145235	As part of its work the EPRG is anxious to construct , and then make widely available to interested parties , an inventory of all case-control studies that are in progress across Europe and that are designed to investigate possible associations between particular conditions and prior exposure to medicinal products .
145236	Investigators conducting such studies are invited to contact the EPRG Project Co-ordinator ( Prof M. D. Rawlins , Wolfson Unit of Clinical Pharmacology , Department of Pharmacological Sciences , University of Newcastle , Newcastle upon Tyne NE2 4HH , UK ) briefly outlining the study ( in not more than 2 to 3 sentences ) , its start date , its planned date of termination , and the projected numbers of cases and controls to be recruited .
145237	Update on SIDS
145238	Although the number of cases of sudden infant death syndrome ( SIDS ) in the UK in 1992 was half that in 1991 ( 456 vs 912 , respectively ) , SIDS remains the commonest cause of death in babies older than 1 week .
145239	Last week the UK Department of Health confirmed its earlier recommendations that the risk of cot death is reduced if infants are laid to sleep on their backs , if they are not exposed to cigarette smoke before or after birth , and if they are not overwrapped or overheated , especially when feverish or unwell .
145240	Preliminary results presented at a meeting organised by the Foundation for the Study of Infant Deaths may provide some leads toward the mechanisms involved in SIDS .
145241	Dr Peter Fleming , Bristol Maternity Hospital , UK , reported that changes in the variability of respiration in response to alterations in room temperature have been found in some normal infants .
145242	In addition , preliminary results of a postoperative study reported by Dr Stewart Petersen , University of Leicester , UK , and Dr Mike Wailoo , Leicester Royal Infirmary , suggest that changes in an infant 's body temperature may precede ( by up to 1 week ) the development of other symptoms of infection that are recognised by parents .
145243	These studies may provide some insight into the roles of overwrapping , overheating , and infections in SIDS .
145244	However , other research suggests that a disturbance of maturation of the brain may be involved .
145245	Pathological dendrite formation in neurons of the substantia nigra has been found in brains of infants who died of SIDS and also in infants with intrauterine growth retardation .
145246	According to Professor Dick van Velzen , Royal Liverpool Children 's Hospital , UK , these changes may be important in the aetiology of SIDS because they occur in an area involved in the control of breathing , heart rate , and temperature .
145247	LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
145248	Is PCR a viable option for population screening ?
145249	SIR , — Theoretically , the polymerase chain reaction ( PCR ) is the most sensitive test for the detection of infectious pathogens , and , in practice , its sensitivity exceeds that of animal transmission studies , which may represent the lower limit of clinical relevance .
145250	For many infectious agents , hepatitis C virus ( HCV ) in particular , the specificity and extreme sensitivity of PCR makes it superior to standard serological tests in the determination of carrier state , and false-negative serological results have led to the suggestion that PCR should replace antibody testing for screening .
145251	However , PCR is expensive and time consuming , and is generally regarded as unsuitable for the mass screening of clinical samples .
145252	By arranging the samples to be tested in a two-dimensional array , either physically or conceptually , pooling the samples in both columns and rows ( figure ) , and doing PCR on the pooled samples and those individual samples found to be positive by ‘ grid referencing ’ , it is possible to increase the efficiency of screening .
145253	Assuming one positive , and both negative reagent and sample controls , are run concurrently , and grid-reference-positive samples are not retested , the screening load of grid-referenced PCR ( the number of samples to be assayed ) increases at 2n+3 , where n is the dimension of the array , while the screening rate ( the number of samples about which information is obtained ) increases at n ( figure , a ) .
145254	Thus , to screen a 20x20 array ( 400 samples ) by grid-referenced PCR , a minimum of 43 individual PCR reactions would need to be run .
145255	Assuming a single positive in the samples tested , the screening multiple ( the ratio between the screening rate and the screening load ) also increases exponentially ( at a rate n/2n+3 ) and in a 2020 array is 400/43 or 9.3 , meaning information is obtained on 9.3 samples for every one tested .
145256	However , the wider application of this approach is limited by the introduction of ‘ test false positives ’ created by the grid-reference system ( figure , b ) .
145257	The number of false positives ( FP ) generated by grid referencing and requiring subsequent PCR is a function of the number of true positives ( P ) , and of the distribution of those positives , but will maximally increase according to the equation FP=PP , meaning that the overall screening load increases at a rate 2n+3+ ( PP ) , and the screening multiple by n/2n+3+ ( PP ) .
145258	The efficiency of grid-referenced PCR , reflected in the screening multiple , therefore declines with increasing prevalence of positives within the samples .
145259	Nevertheless , at a positive prevalence of 1% in a 2020 array , a screening multiple of &gt;6 can be achieved : useful information is obtained on 6 samples for every one assayed .
145260	Sensitivity , a major concern when screening in a clinical setting , would decline as an inverse function of n , at rate 1/n ( and is a function of Vap/Vp , where Vap is the volume of the pooled sample assayed and Vp the pooled volume ) , assuming DNA/RNA is extracted from the same volume of pooled serum as standard PCR assays .
145261	Although the loss of sensitivity inherent in grid-referenced PCR needs to be addressed , it is possible that it will not be a major issue ; even patients with chronic hepatitis C , who frequently have low levels of viraemia , generally have circulating levels of virus orders of magnitude greater than the lower limits of detection by PCR , and levels of hepatitis B virus DNA in chronic carriers are orders of magnitude greater still .
145262	This methodology might be applicable to large-scale seroepidemiological studies of pathogens found at low prevalence within populations .
145263	Immunoglobulin preparations , acutegraft-versus-host disease , and infectionafter marrow transplant
145264	SIR , — Dr Blasczyk and colleagues ( March 27 , p 789 ) describe the variable content of soluble CD4 , CD8 , and HLA class I and II molecules in commercial preparations of intravenous immunoglobulin ( IVIG ) .
145265	Although the benefit of IVIG in terms of reduced infection and acute graft-versus-host disease ( GVHD ) has been shown among recipients of allogeneic marrow transplants , the mechanism of action , and the optimal dose and preparation , remain undefined .
145266	At Georgetown University Hospital between 1987 and 1992 , 41 patients undergoing HLA-genotypically-identical sibling donor transplant received high dose IVIG for infection and GVHD prophylaxis , and survived at least 30 days after the transplant .
145267	Twenty-two patients received Gamimune N ( Cutter/Miles ) at a dose of 200–500 mg/kg per week beginning on day 8 until day +28 , then every other week until day +100 .
145268	Subsequently , the toxicities and pharmacokinetics of continuous infusion ( CI ) IVIG of Gammagard ( Baxter/Hyland ) in 19 patients at a dose of 1000 mg/kg on day 8 , then 500 mg/kg per week until day +100 were measured .
145269	GVHD and antimicrobial prophylaxis were the same for all patients .
145270	Although a lower incidence of bacterial and fungal infections was observed among the CI Gammagard-treated group , there was also an increased incidence of GVHD grade II or more ( table ) .
145271	Since the dose ( and serum concentrations achieved ) were higher with CI Gammagard , the decreased rate of infection might be explained by higher specific antibody concentrations .
145272	The increase in acute GVHD in this group , however , was unexpected .
145273	Although these data must be interpreted with caution given the non-randomised nature of the studies , and the heterogeneous group of diseases among the two patient groups , it is intriguing to speculate that non-specific immunosuppression might occur as a result of the increased concentration of soluble HLA molecules in Gamimune N relative to Gammagard .
145274	As Blasczyk et al suggest , such molecules might interfere with the association between HLA molecules expressed on antigen-presenting cells and corresponding HLA-restricted T cells , leading to less severe GVHD .
145275	Alternatively , the increased concentration of soluble CD4 and CD8 in Gammagard relative to Gamimune N might stimulate cells with the appropriate receptors , leading to more severe GVHD .
145276	Future trials comparing the most commonly used IVIG preparations in marrow transplantation should measure not only differences in infection but in the incidence of GVHD , to further elucidate the mechanism of immune changes due to IVIG .
145277	Determination of genetic sex by PCRamplification of Y-chromosome-specificsequences
145278	SIR , — Gender verification of Olympic athletes has been a matter for discussion since the first analyses were done in Mexico in 1968 .
145279	Recently , the International Olympic Committee ( IOC ) decided to use a new technique , the polymerase chain reaction ( PCR ) , to detect Y-chromosome-specific sequences ( Y-PCR ) .
145280	Since this decision has caused controversy , we thought it important to disclose the details and results of the analysis used at the Barcelona Olympic Games .
145281	Several Y-specific genes have been used for sex typing .
145282	Evidence from laboratory animals supports the idea that the testis determining factor is the product of the SRY gene .
145283	For this reason , SRY and another Y-specific gene , DYZ , were chosen as targets .
145284	As a first step , the presence of DYZ1 was determined with lysates of buccal smears from female competitors and two specific primers .
145285	Details of the protocol will be published elsewhere .
145286	As an internal control , co-amplification of a sequence specific for mitochondrial DNA was done .
145287	In our previous studies , amplification of DYZ-specific sequences was detected in all 89 male samples and in none of 1629 female samples .
145288	However , when samples from 2406 female competitors in Barcelona were analysed , 11 ( 0.46% ) had a positive result .
145289	In a second screening , SRY and DYZ1 were amplified from purified DNA from these 11 samples .
145290	Amplification of the DYZ1-specific sequence was detected in 11 samples , as expected ; however , only 5 contained SRY .
145291	The IOC Medical Commission criteria state that a sample is positive only if both SRY and DYZ1 are found .
145292	Only these 5 athletes were invited to attend for a medical examinaton .
145293	Details have not been disclosed but morphological abnormalities were observed in 4 , the other athlete refused ( Dr Eduardo Hay , IOC Medical Commission , personal communication ) .
145294	The findings are strictly confidential and we do not know if these athletes were allowed to compete .
145295	In some cases , such as ‘ male pseudohermaphroditism ’ , genetic sex does not coincide with phenotypic or physiological sex .
145296	The IOC Medical Commission was aware of this , and , for this reason , the presence of a Y chromosome was not a reason for exclusion ; a complete physical examination was done before any decision about eligibility .
145297	The advantages of Y-PCR over the test used in the past have been described .
145298	We believe that Y-PCR testing , followed by a physical examination of positive cases , is a valid method of verifying the genetic sex of large numbers of people .
145299	Several experts have proposed that the physical examination be carried out without previous screening .
145300	We think , however , that most athletes would find a gynaecological examination purely for gender verification a humiliating experience .
145301	Whatever method is chosen in the future , extreme care will have to be taken to preserve confidentiality before and after the final decision .
145302	Non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriaevar gravis in England
145303	SIR , — Major Sloss and Col Faithfull-Davies ' report ( April 17 , p 1021 ) of non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae var gravis among military personnel re-emphasises the importance of screening for C diphtheriae .
145304	However , we point out that the Diphtheria Reference Laboratory is not part of the Communicable Disease Surveillance Centre , Colindale , as they suggest .
145305	The correct designation is the Diphtheria ( WHO ) Reference Unit , Respiratory and Systemic Infection Laboratory , Central Public Health Laboratory .
145306	The number of isolations of non-toxigenic C diphtheriae var gravis referred to the unit from laboratories that continue to screen all throat swabs for C diphtheriae has increased fivefold from 1990 to 1992 .
145307	Since January , 1992 , 54% ( 76/140 ) of referrals have belonged to this biotype .
145308	These isolates have mostly been referred from children and young adults ( aged 5–35 years ) with pharyngitis .
145309	A recent report by Wilson and colleagues drew attention to the isolation of non-toxigenic C diphtheriae var gravis from patients attending a genitourinary medicine ( GUM ) clinic at a London hospital .
145310	However , most isolates referred to the reference unit have no apparent association with GUM clinics .
145311	A striking increase in this biotype has also been recorded elsewhere , including 7 cases of endocarditis in Australia .
145312	The diphtheria laboratory has only examined one isolate of non-toxigenic C diphtheriae var gravis isolated from blood cultures of a patient in England .
145313	This seems to be the first manifestation of invasive disease referred to the reference unit by a laboratory in the UK .
145314	Molecular epidemiological studies have shown that geographical heterogeneity exists between isolates and that numerous clones ( defined by restriction fragment-length polymorphism analysis of rRNA genes ) seem to be circulating .
145315	Toxin characterisation studies have demonstrated the absence of the structural gene for diphtheria toxin and also in-vitro and in-vivo expression of the protein .
145316	There is no information on the carriage rates for this organism but the apparent increase is of concern , as is its potential to cause invasive disease in some patients .
145317	Disappearance of antibodies to HPV 16 E7after treatment for cervical cancer
145318	SIR , — Dr Jha and colleagues ( May 1 , p 1116 ) report antibodies against human papillomavirus ( HPV ) 16 E7 peptide ( originally reported by Mueller et al ) among women who had been diagnosed with cervical carcinoma on average 4 years before being contacted for donation of a serum sample .
145319	The use of cases with a history of disease , rather than incident cases , is fraught with systematic biases .
145320	The most obvious difficulty is whether antibody titres change after diagnosis and treatment , either as a result of curative treatment with removal of the antigenic stimulus , or of progression of disease and concomitant immunosuppression .
145321	To examine these issues , Lehtinen and co-workers obtained serum samples from 28 patients with incident cervical cancer who were admitted to Helsinki University Hospital , Finland .
145322	Serum samples were obtained both before treatment and at regular intervals during follow-up of up to 15 months .
145323	These patients and their serological reactions to various HPV and herpes simplex virus type 2 ( HSV-2 ) antigens have been reported in detail .
145324	I analysed serum samples from these patients for antibodies against the HPV 16 E7 peptide used by Jha et al .
145325	With the aim of achieving comparability of methods , the E7 peptide as well as positive and negative reference sera were obtained from Dr Mueller .
145326	5/28 patients were strongly positive ( enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay [ ELISA ] titre &gt;1/600 ) for IgG to the E7 peptide .
145327	In 3/5 patients , E7 antibody titres declined during follow-up , and in the other 2 patients the antibodies were undetectable after 1 year ( figure ) .
145328	The effect of disappearing seropositivity with time elapsed since diagnosis and treatment probably resulted in an underestimation of relative risks in Jha 's study .
145329	In addition , Jha and colleagues probably selectively excluded patients with progressive disease , since a high proportion of such patients will be dead within 4 years after diagnosis .
145330	The selective exclusion of patients with progressive cancer introduces an additional systematic error , although it can not a priori be said whether this would tend to underestimate or exaggerate relative risks .
145331	Further , cervical cancer treatment will typically include radiotherapy , which will result in release of autoantigens and generation of autoantibodies that can cause background difficulties in various serological assays .
145332	Thus , if a large proportion of cases , but no controls , have received radiotherapy , there will also be a systematic bias that will tend to exaggerate relative risks .
145333	It is questionable whether the study of patients with a history of having been diagnosed with cervical cancer can form the basis for conclusions about the seroepidemiology of this disease .
145334	It is unfortunate that Jha et al do not point out the disadvantages of not using incident cases , nor try to estimate the magnitude of the systematic errors thus introduced .
145335	Cyclic guanosine monophosphate in heartfailure
145336	SIR , — Dr Lerman and colleagues ' report ( May 1 , p 1105 ) on circulating N-terminal atrial natriuretic peptide as a marker for symptomless left-ventricular dysfunction , and your accompanying commentary by Professor Barnett on the diagnosis of symptomless left-ventricular dysfunction , prompt us to draw attention to another promising analyte for diagnosing and monitoring heart failure — cyclic guanosine monophosphate ( cGMP ) .
145337	Once released from the heart , natriuretic peptides exert potent direct vasodilator and natriuretic actions by virtue of their ability to increase their intracellular second messenger cGMP .
145338	Since cGMP is extruded from cells after interaction with atrial natriuretic peptide ( ANP ) or brain natriuretic peptide ( BNP ) , it is a possible marker for natriuretic peptides .
145339	In patients with heart failure , close correlations have been described between cGMP and ANP plasma concentrations .
145340	Both ANP and cGMP correlate closely with the severity of congestive heart failure .
145341	In addition , exogenously administered ANP raised plasma cGMP concentration in accordance with its physiological effects .
145342	Because in plasma cGMP has a longer half-life ( 15 min ) than ANP ( 1–2 min ) , cGMP can be regarded as a more sensitive marker for ANP release than ANP itself in many situations .
145343	Routine laboratory use of ANP and other natriuretic peptides in heart failure hints at difficulties with storage , because these peptides are highly susceptible to degradation under most storage conditions .
145344	By contrast , even at room temperature cGMP is stable for at least five days in plasma samples containing edetic acid .
145345	Our results indicate that ethanol extraction of plasma samples before measurement of cGMP is not necessary ( correlation of values with and without previous ethanol extraction : r=0.91 , p=0.0001 , n=52 ) .
145346	We could demonstrate that cGMP yields high sensitivity ( 94.2% ) and specificity ( 93.7% ) for cardiac diseases in the absence of severe renal functional impairment .
145347	Symptom-limited ergometric exercise testing increases the diagnostic sensitivity of cGMP for symptomless heart dysfunction ( see figure ) .
145348	Before exercise , cGMP concentrations of New York Heart Association ( NYHA ) class I patients were only slightly raised and did not differ significantly from concentrations of healthy controls or patients with non-cardiac diseases .
145349	By contrast , 30 min after finishing ergometric exercise testing , cGMP in NYHA I patients was significantly higher than in controls .
145350	The high diagnostic efficiency of cGMP , its stability , and the possibility of direct cGMP determination in plasma samples lead us to conclude that in patients with heart failure measurement of cGMP is an alternative to measurement of natriuretic peptides for routine clinical laboratory medicine .
145351	Misleading herbal Ayurvedic brand name
145352	SIR , — Herbal medicines are being used by many patients in India and Europe .
145353	Drugs from the ancient system of medicine Ayurveda are popular in India , and are believed to be safe because of their long history of use and their natural origin .
145354	However , clinically important interactions between Ayurvedic medicines and modern medicines have been recorded .
145355	I report another difficulty that can arise from a belief in safety of Ayurvedic medicines and misleading brand names .
145356	Pain relieving medicines such as aspirin or ibuprofen are used for headache , pain , and arthritis .
145357	Prolonged use of these medicines is known to harm the gastric mucosa .
145358	If used by a person with pre-existing ulcer , the damage can be serious and cause severe bleeding .
145359	Doctors warn patients and take necessary precautions .
145360	I have noticed a preparation , Vendana Nigraha Rasa , which is recommended for pain relief by several lay people .
145361	These words are Sanskrit ( ancient Indian language ) , and vendana means pain , nigraha determination , and Rasa juice .
145362	The Sanskrit words give a false sense of the product being Ayurvedic and hence herbal and safe .
145363	Actually , its main ingredients are aspirin ( 530 mg ) and paracetamol ( 100 mg ) .
145364	Like other Ayurvedic preparations the drug is effective , which is not surprising since it contains almost double the quantity of aspirin used in normal aspirin tablets .
145365	I am aware of one educated patient , with known duodenal ulcer , who had started taking this medicine for headache , believing it to be Ayurvedic and despite the facts that it is labelled as containing 530 mg aspirin and 100 mg paracetamol and that he had been instructed by his doctor to refrain from all pain-relieving medications like aspirin .
145366	In a survey of pharmacies , I have not come across any other such misbranded medications .
145367	Doctors , patients , and law-enforcing authorities should take a note of this warning and patients should ascertain that the Ayurvedic medicines they are taking do not contain anything other than Ayurvedic medicine .
145368	Lack of association between myelin basicprotein gene microsatellite and multiplesclerosis
145369	SIR , — Dr Rose and colleagues ( May 8 , p 1179 ) report that a tetranucleotide repeat polymorphism , 5 to the myelin basic protein ( MBP ) gene , is not genetically linked with familial multiple sclerosis ( MS ) .
145370	This finding is in contrast to previous population-based studies by Boylan et al and Tienari et al and their co-workers , in which this locus was shown to be associated with MS .
145371	The Finnish study also demonstrated linkage in families said to have clinical MS .
145372	However , both these studies used a low resolution technique to type a complex tetranucleotide repeat polymorphism , and thus alleles assigned the same fragment length may be genetically heterogeneous .
145373	This difficulty was recognised by Boylan et al .
145374	A much improved method for typing this polymorphism has since been reported .
145375	This procedure enables accurate discrimination of allele sizes for a pair of tetranucleotide repeats at the 5 end of this complex repeat , and is the method used by Rose and colleagues .
145376	We have also used this refined method to type alleles of the A and B loci of this MBP marker in 122 unrelated patients with clinically definite MS from neurology clinics in Belfast and Coleraine and 106 blood donor controls .
145377	The table shows the allele frequencies for both the A and B loci in the healthy and MS populations .
145378	The frequencies for all the alleles of both markers are very similar in the two populations and there is no allelic association with MS .
145379	Analysis of genotype frequencies in both groups also failed to reveal any genotypic association with MS .
145380	Thus this study , in the Northern Ireland MS population , confirms the work of Rose and colleagues , and infers that the myelin basic protein gene is not a candidate for conferring susceptibility to MS .
145381	SIR , — In not accepting our explanation ( May 15 , p 1286 ) for the difference between the November , 1988 , and January , 1990 , forecasts for AIDS incidence in England and Wales — namely , a slowing down in the rate of transmission of HIV among homosexual men — Professor Stewart ( p 1287 ) states that we are not reading the data correctly .
145382	The data he cites are misleading or irrelevant and his line of argument is contradictory .
145383	Stewart uses quarterly surveillance data to suggest that new reports of AIDS in homosexual men increased by 62% ( from 785 to 1268 ) in late 1987 to early 1988 , and that there was subsequently a further rise of 50% .
145384	He arrived at these numbers by comparing reported AIDS cases in homosexual/bisexual males for the UK in 1986 and 1987 ( 785 ) with reports for 1988 and 1989 ( 1268 ) and for 1990 and 1991 ( 1907 ) .
145385	Grouping data in this way obscures the underlying trend .
145386	The figure summarises data for England and Wales ( excluding visitors ) .
145387	Locally weighted scatter plot smoothing illustrates the slowing of the rate of increase in AIDS incidence in homosexual/bisexual males , beginning in 1987 and becoming more striking in 1988 .
145388	The trend in total AIDS incidence reflects this change .
145389	Stewart also implies that our statement could be based upon the ‘ impressive 30% drop in the number of homosexual men serotesting positively for HIV in late 1987 to early 1988 ’ .
145390	This drop is largely irrelevant because the long incubation period of 10 years or more between HIV-1 infection and AIDS onset results in a complex relation between the time of HIV-1 infection diagnosis and AIDS incubation period .
145391	In a symptom-free person diagnosis of HIV-1 infection depends on factors such as risk recognition , willingness to have an HIV-1 test , and test accessibility , all of which changed during the 1980s .
145392	The amount of HIV-1 testing , the proportion found infected when first having an HIV-1 test , and the numbers of HIV-1 infections diagnosed among homosexual/bisexual men between 1985 and 1989 , are a poor guide to the underlying incidence of HIV-1 infections and should not be used to interpret the AIDS incidence curve directly .
145393	We find a contradiction in Stewart 's statement that the sharp rise in ( AIDS ) reports in 1987–88 was statistically merely a blip .
145394	The effect of the introduction of the 1987 expanded AIDS case definition was much less in England and Wales than elsewhere and did not result in a sharp rise in incidence among homosexual/bisexual men ( figure ) .
145395	Stewart does not successfully refute the statement that the principal reason for the difference between the 1988 and 1990 forecasts was the reduction in HIV transmission among homosexual/bisexual men in the mid-1980s , the extent of which only became apparent between the reports .
145396	Opportunistic infections and CD4lymphocytopenia with interferon treatmentin HIV-1 infected patients
145397	SIR , — Dr Vento and colleagues ( April 10 , p 958 ) reported a decline of CD4 cells after interferon ( IFN ) treatment in HIV-1 infection .
145398	We recently observed two cases of such cytopenia complicated by opportunistic infections .
145399	Case 1 was a female intravenous drug user , 32 , and seropositive since 1987 .
145400	IFN treatment ( IFN-2a , Roferon , Roche ) was started in August , 1992 , for chronic viral hepatitis C. Alanine aminotransferase ( ALT ) was 69 IU/L , CD4 cells 310/L , and serum p24 antigen was negative .
145401	Three months later , the patient had fever and headache which led to the diagnosis of cerebral toxoplasmosis with multiple cerebral abscesses .
145402	CD4 cells were 130/L , and serum p24 antigen was strongly positive ( 242 pg/ml ) .
145403	ALT was normal .
145404	IFN treatment was stopped .
145405	The patient is presently well and taking zidovudine , with a CD4 cell count of 90/mm .
145406	Case 2 was a male intravenous drug user , 32 , and seropositive since 1986 .
145407	IFN was started in February , 1993 , for chronic viral hepatitis C. ALT was 180 IU/L , CD4 cells 600/L , and serum p24 antigen was negative .
145408	Six weeks later , the patient was febrile , with perineal pain and oral candidosis .
145409	Biopsy and culture of anal ulcers showed anorectal tuberculosis .
145410	CD4 cells were 134/L and serum p24 antigen was negative .
145411	ALT was 72 IU/L .
145412	The patient is now well and taking four antituberculous antibiotics and zidovudine .
145413	None of Vento 's three patients developed AIDS during IFN therapy .
145414	We report here 2 cases of opportunistic infections occurring after 3 months and 6 weeks , respectively , of IFN given for chronic viral hepatitis C in intravenous drug using seropositive patients .
145415	Most HIV-positive intravenous drug users are also infected by hepatitis C virus .
145416	IFN treatment in these patients must take into consideration the CD4 cell count and HLA haplotypes .
145417	SIR , — Most commentators would describe ‘ life-terminating acts without explicit request of patient ’ ( LAWER ) as non-voluntary euthanasia but the Dutch do not because euthanasia was defined for the Remmelink report only as ‘ intentionally taking the life of a person upon his or her explicit request by someone else than the person concerned ’ .
145418	The only legal category for LAWER in the Netherlands , as elsewhere , is murder .
145419	The patients were incompetent , generally unconscious , and incapable of consent .
145420	In 59% ‘ some information ’ was available about the patient 's possible wishes ; in 30% no medical consultation had taken place ; in nearly 20% the family was not told what was happening ; and in 40% , the killing was at the family 's request .
145421	The three illustrative cases call for comment .
145422	In the woman with bone metastases the pain became ‘ more and more difficult to relieve with opioids ’ , not surprisingly since such pain is better treated with other analgesics .
145423	Consciousness deteriorated and , since the pain ‘ could no longer be relieved ’ , it was decided to kill her with a large dose of opioids .
145424	What effect on pain might , say , three-quarters of the lethal dose have had ?
145425	One reason for this action was ‘ unbearable suffering ’ .
145426	The patient was unconscious .
145427	Whose suffering ?
145428	In the second case consciousness also deteriorated rapidly .
145429	She had a respiratory infection and one reason for life termination was ‘ the threat of asphyxia ’ — so she was given high-dose opioids , which ensured that she died of asphyxia .
145430	The permanently unconscious man , who was not suffering , was killed with a lethal injection , in part because of his poor quality of life .
145431	Whatever other reasons may have existed — and however unpleasant it may be to be reminded of it — this is the same reason used in Germany in the 1930s .
145432	In the early 1970s , when the Dutch first got the legal go-ahead on medical killing , the British were developing palliative care — and so the two nations have continued .
145433	Because there is no organised palliative care in the Netherlands , Dr Pijnenborg and her colleagues think ‘ that a doctor 's duty to preserve life and to alleviate suffering are in conflict ’ , and refer to the injustice that a patient must ‘ suffer to the end ’ .
145434	But there is only injustice when preventable suffering is allowed to persist to the point where a person would rather be dead .
145435	The final irony comes with the observation that future safeguards ‘ must include optimal palliative care ’ .
145436	SIR , — Dr Pijnenborg and colleagues state that LAWER ‘ complicates ’ the debate but does not challenge the moral justifiability of euthanasia .
145437	We disagree : LAWER accentuates the moral problems doctors face once euthanasia is accepted as normal medical practice .
145438	There are methodological problems with this study .
145439	9% of physicians refused to participate and only 322 of the 405 included did take part .
145440	Is it correct to ignore the attitudes and practices of these other physicians ?
145441	Second , there are difficulties in interpreting ‘ non-explicit requests ’ .
145442	At best they are uncertain and may well reflect the impressions and attitudes of the attending physicians .
145443	The physician ‘ knew the patient ’ but is this type of knowledge morally relevant when deciding on life-terminating acts ?
145444	One-third of the specialists ‘ knew their patient less than a month ’ , hardly a reassuring foundation for insight into patients ' non-explicit wishes .
145445	Pijnenborg et al point out that ‘ many doctors ’ participate in and accept the practice and they claim that the practice has been stable over the years and assume that it may be less in future .
145446	In the light of the methodological weaknesses and the fact that euthanasia without explicit requests was not permitted ( but still yielded 1000 cases per year ) we are not convinced that LAWER has not increased in frequency .
145447	That many doctors condone this practice does not in itself indicate any moral justification .
145448	The life-shortening effect in LAWER is claimed to be ‘ smaller than that in euthanasia because the patients usually have only a few hours or days to live ’ .
145449	Is this shorter time frame relevant morally ?
145450	Dutch investigators refer to poor quality of life and to the injustice of suffering .
145451	Is it the responsibility of medicine to compensate for poor quality of life or to eliminate injustices by non-consenting life-terminating acts — or is death to be seen as a therapy ?
145452	We are told medical decisions at the end of life ( MDEL ) will increase in importance with demographic shifts towards older populations , with the increasing proportions of cancer and with the growth of life prolonging technologies'' .
145453	We agree that medical technology complicates end of life decisions , but do not see how old age and cancer should indicate an increased use of MDEL or LAWER .
145454	SIR , — The details of the circumstances of LAWER lead Dr L. Pijnenborg and colleagues to disturbing conclusions .
145455	First , LAWER is viewed as the caring response of doctor and relatives for the patient , whose wishes , they feel ‘ confident ’ , would have been for life to have been ended .
145456	What gives the doctor the certainty that he knows the mind of his patient ?
145457	Human beings reserve the right to alter and change views .
145458	Moreover , if the answer is knowledge of the patient over time , what of the 2.3% of general practitioners and 31.3% of specialists who carried out LAWER on patients whom they knew for less than one month ?
145459	Second , should LAWER be viewed as an acceptable outcome of the doctor 's responsibility towards well-known patients in great pain but unable to express wishes ?
145460	The present state of the hospice movement and continuing research on pain relief make us ask , ‘ is optimum pain alleviation being sought ? ’
145461	It is up to the medical profession to take stock of advances in this aspect of practice .
145462	Yet , if pain remains , who would be so bold as to decide when the patient 's limit of tolerance has been reached ?
145463	If there is no blanket strategy that can be applied to all , then more and better individualised pain care is needed .
145464	Third , the logical ramifications of LAWER must be considered .
145465	If it is acceptable to take away the lives of some , then we can no longer say that all human life is equally important and valued .
145466	How can we then value life ?
145467	The quality of life that is appropriate and fitting for the neonate , young adult , handicapped man , and elderly woman are different .
145468	Therefore , we must have a clear picture of the patients ' beliefs and attitudes towards life .
145469	What are we then to make of the 41% of LAWER that took place without discussion or the patient 's previous wishes being made known ?
145470	Fourth , Pijnenborg and colleagues suggest that there is no evidence that the frequency of LAWER will increase , and thus it need not be the ‘ thin edge of the wedge ’ .
145471	If this is so , is it not strange that already 2% of physicians carrying out LAWER did not consult anyone ?
145472	Interviews with doctors who practise euthanasia have shown that they resort to LAWER when they have neither the courage nor cruelty to talk openly with patients , relatives , or colleagues .
145473	Finally , it is fascinating to discover that Pijnenborg and colleagues are not able to define LAWER as murder or medical practice .
145474	How then are we to view the procedure ?
145475	Furthermore , is it not rash to say that it is to be carried out only in the patients ' best interests ?
145476	It does seem rather odd to say that death is for the good of the person involved .
145477	It is far from clear how we can compare a situation of living with one of absence of sensation and life itself .
145478	SIR , — Dr Pijnenborg and colleagues ' description of LAWER resembles the dictionary definition of murder ( ‘ unlawful killing of a human being on purpose ’ ) .
145479	Their reasoning — that ‘ when all safeguards are respected and the best interests of the patient are taken into account , it is certainly not murder ’ — parallels the apparent logic behind the Soviet cleansing of antisocialist elements , the Indian practice of murder/suicide of widows , and the infanticide that I observed among the Tsamai in south-west Ethiopia .
145480	Dutch euthanasia practice is legalised and therefore becomes a collective responsibility but , as with war crimes , collective responsibility does not free the actor ( the physician ) from personal accountability .
145481	Increased cerebral blood volume associatedwith pneumothorax in preterm infant
145482	SIR , — Pneumothorax has been shown to be associated with intracranial haemorrhage in the newborn .
145483	There is evidence from observational studies in newborn infants , and experiments in animals that the pathogenesis linking these two conditions is venous congestion .
145484	An unexpected increase in cerebral blood volume ( CBV ) was observed during mechanical ventilation of a premature infant suffering from hyaline membrane disease .
145485	The infant was monitored continously with near-infrared spectroscopy on days 1 and 2 of life .
145486	Changes in CBV were recorded continuously by a cerebral oxygen monitor 105 Kritikon ( Johnson &amp; Johnson ) .
145487	Absolute values of CBV were determined repetitively according to the method proposed by Wyatt .
145488	On day 1 , CBV remained stable whereas on day 2 it increased .
145489	At the end of day 2 , pneumothorax was diagnosed .
145490	Heart rate , transcutaneous carbon dioxide tension , arterial saturation , and mean arterial blood pressure did not change .
145491	This observation suggests that pneumothorax can influence cerebral haemodynamics without affecting heart rate , blood pressure , and blood gases .
145492	Detection of changes in cerebral haemodynamics by near-infrared spectroscopy allows early intervention to prevent intracranial haemorrhage .
145493	Limitations of pulse oximetry
145494	SIR , — Dr John and Dr Peacock ( April 24 , p 1093 ) report delayed recognition of ventilatory failure in 3 cases of severe hypercarbia monitored by pulse oximetry ( SpO ) .
145495	We observed limitations of SpO in 6 patients treated after inhalation of carbon monoxide ( CO ) , whose carboxyhaemoglobin ( COHb ) on admission ranged between 29% and 41% .
145496	2 female ( aged 87 and 71 years ) and 1 male patients ( 70 ) were admitted after they complained of headache , dizziness , vertigo , and ataxia , and CO-poisoning was suspected .
145497	1 h after admission ( about 4 h after the start of symptoms ) the male patient had a non-Q-wave myocardial infarction despite oxygen administration .
145498	He was transferred for further treatment to a medical ward , and the other 2 patients were discharged .
145499	2 further patients ( 1 man aged 60 and 1 woman of 61 ) were brought to our institution after exposure to CO at the home of an older relative who had died .
145500	Their symptoms were headache and nausea .
145501	Oxygen was given and both patients made an uneventful recovery .
145502	The sixth patient was a 33-year-old man who was admitted after a suicide attempt by inhalation of car engine exhaust fumes and ingestion of about 20 mg of flunitrazepam .
145503	On admission he was intubated , haemodynamically stable , and unresponsive to pain .
145504	He was mechanically ventilated with 100% oxygen and eventually extubated after intravenous flumazenil .
145505	After initiation of psychiatric care and normalisation of a moderate rhabdomyolysis ( peak creatine kinase 4120 U/L ) the patient was discharged .
145506	Serial measurements of COHb ( IL 482 CO-Oximeter , Instrumentation Laboratory , USA ) were done hourly in all 6 patients until the index became normal , and arterial blood pressure , heart rate , and SpO were monitored ( peripheral oxygen saturation by M1020 module , Hewlett Packard , USA ) .
145507	The figure shows mean COHb values with corresponding SpO .
145508	At all 18 measurements , the mean SpO value was above 91% , which would be readily accepted as sufficient oxygenation .
145509	Decreasing COHb values led to a slight increase of SpO , as would be expected by the formula SpO= ( OHb+0.9COHb ) /total Hb100% , according to Tremper and Barker .
145510	The increasing availability of pulse oximetry in intensive care units may lead to a false interpretation of oxygen transport capacity in cases of CO poisoning , especially if SpO is between 91% and 98% .
145511	Physicians should be aware that the diagnosis of CO poisoning still depends on a high degree of clinical suspicion and direct measurement of CO .
145512	Increased serum tumour necrosis factor during transient remission in acute leukaemia
145513	SIR , — Spontaneous remission of acute leukaemia is unusual .
145514	Most instances have been associated with infection , blood transfusion , or termination of pregnancy .
145515	The mechanism is unknown , although it has been suggested that activation of tumour necrosis factor ( TNF ) may be responsible .
145516	A 72-year-old woman had a transient remission of acute undifferentiated leukaemia coinciding with a pneumonia , during which raised concentrations of TNF were found .
145517	She was admitted to hospital in September , 1991 , because of fever , productive cough , and weakness .
145518	She had a history of insulin-dependent diabetes and hypertension .
145519	Physical examination was normal .
145520	Blood values were : haemoglobin 105 g/L , mean corpuscular volume 89 m , white blood cells 1.410/L ( 12% neutrophils , 4% band forms , 80% lymphocytes , 4% eosinophils ) , and platelets 20210/L .
145521	The bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular , with 71% of blast cells .
145522	Cytochemistry for myeloperoxidase and esterases was negative .
145523	Immunological marker studies of bone marrow ( immunoalkaline phosphatase ) showed CD45 and HLA-DR positivity in blast cells , whereas CD14 , CD15 , CD7 , CD19 , and CD20 were negative .
145524	Cytogenetic analysis of the bone marrow showed 3n hyperdiploidy ( 15 evaluable metaphases ) .
145525	Due to the age of the patient and the medical history , treatment with low-dose daunorubicin ( 55 mg/m per day for 2 days ) and cytoarabine ( 100 mg/m per day in continous intravenous infusion for 5 days ) was given .
145526	A bone marrow aspirate 15 days after the end of chemotherapy was hypocellular with 62% blast cells .
145527	The patient was followed up as an outpatient , and only supportive treatment with packed red cells given .
145528	6 months later she was readmitted with pneumonia .
145529	The blood , urine , and sputum cultures were negative .
145530	Ceftazidime , aztreonam , erythromycin , and amphotericin B were given .
145531	The pneumonia resolved in 18 days .
145532	Staphylococcus epidermidis was isolated in two blood cultures .
145533	A bone marrow aspirate showed 64% blast cells .
145534	The patient was discharged without any further treatment .
145535	After two weeks the general health of the patient improved , and her blood values were : haemoglobin 145 g/L , mean corpuscular volume 88 m , white blood cells 4.510/L ( 64% neutrophils , 1% basophil , 3% eosinophils , 32% lymphocytes ) , and platelets 23910/L .
145536	A bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular .

145538	Only 9% of blast cells were seen .
145539	In the cytogenetic study only 3 metaphases were evaluable , 2 of them being normal and the other 3n .
145540	The patient remained symptom-free for 5 months , until her health worsened .
145541	The blood showed haemoglobin 115 g/L , mean corpuscular volume 92 m , white blood cells 1.610/L , and platelets 13010/L .
145542	The bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular , with 40% of blast cells .
145543	A phenotype study of blast cells showed positivity for HLA-DR , tdT and CD45 , CD68 , and antimyeloperoxidase monoclonal antibodies .
145544	TNF serum concentrations were retrospectively measured in samples taken during her illness .
145545	At the time of diagnosis of leukaemia the TNF was 3 pg/mL ; during her pneumonia , 40 pg/mL ; 2 months after , 8 pg/mL ; and 5 months after , 7 pg/mL .
145546	The transient remission was not due to chemotherapy given 7 months before , without response , and coincided with pneumonia and S epidermidis bacteraemia .
145547	Several cases of spontaneous remission in acute leukaemia have been described in association with bacterial or viral infections .
145548	The most interesting feature in this patient was the inverse relationship between TNF and the number of bone marrow blast cells .
145549	TNF is a cytokine that regulates cell proliferation and differentiation , and takes part in the immune response .
145550	For this reason , TNF can act as an antineoplastic agent .
145551	The relation between high activity of TNF and partial remission of leukemia in the patient reported suggests that TNF could have influenced the transient inhibition of blast cell proliferation .
145552	Sudden infant death associated withdefective oxidative phosphorylation
145553	SIR , — Sudden infant death preceeded by a fulminant hepatocellular disease has been described in children with inborn errors of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation , such as medium-chain acylCoA dehydrogenase deficiency .
145554	Until now there have been few reports on hepatic failure caused by disorders of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation .

145556	The neonates described by Cormier et al , also with cytochrome c oxidase deficiency , had liver disease associated with repeated episodes of ketoacidotic coma .
145557	We report a formerly healthy boy who suddenly died at 11 months after a Reye-like syndrome .
145558	His older sister had died at the age of 6 months after an identical clinical course .
145559	The boy was screened for inborn errors , with negative results .
145560	His medical history was unremarkable until the day before admission .
145561	Early in the afternoon , he became ill with fever and vomiting , and refused feeding .
145562	A general practitioner diagnosed otitis media and prescribed nose-drops .
145563	At 2300 h the boy was in a deep sleep and could hardly be awakened .
145564	Next morning he was found comatose and taken to hospital .
145565	There was severe hypoglycaemia ( 0.7 mmol/L ) , a moderately increased lactate ( 2.4 mmol/L ) , normal pyruvate ( 130 mol/L ) , and hyperammonaemia ( 240 mol/L ) .
145566	Hypoglycaemia was corrected and artificial ventilation started , and he was brought to our clinic .

145571	During the next few hours , he had multiple convulsions .

145573	Necropsy was done within an hour of death .
145574	The liver showed marked steatosis .
145575	Investigation of the fatty acid oxidative capacity in muscle and liver was normal .
145576	Finally , we determined the activities of the respiratory chain enzymes in skeletal muscle .
145577	The results were compatible with a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorders caused by a defect in the coenzyme Q region of the respiratory chain ( table ) .
145578	Most probably the boy 's sister had the same biochemical defect .
145579	At necropsy , she had the same abnormalities , although the activities of respiratory chain enzymes were not examined .
145580	Routine metabolic screening of urine does not fully guarantee the absence of an oxidative phosphorylation disorder .

145591	Triazolam safety
145592	SIR , — Dr Jonas of Upjohn ( May 1 , p 1150 ) claims that my summary of the FDA Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on triazolam was highly selective .
145593	The FDA did not ban the drug , but it did find the 0.5 mg dose excessive and had safety concerns about 0.25 mg .
145594	All the FDA reservations and warnings occurred despite in-house differences of opinion about triazolam 's safety .
145595	The FDA Division of Epidemiology and Surveillance has consistently held over the past six years that triazolam produces many more and more severe psychiatric adverse reactions than comparable benzodiazepines .
145596	The Division of Neuropharmacologic Drug Products disagree ; but this group was responsible for originally approving the use of the 0.5 mg dose in the USA , over the objections of the FDA 's own monitors .
145597	In 1988 , following the ban on the 0.5 mg dose form in France , Italy , and West Germany , the FDA allowed Upjohn to reduce their recommended starting dose to 0.25 mg .
145598	In 1989 , on the basis of data from its Division of Epidemiology and Surveillance , the FDA required stronger warnings , stating that triazolam presented a greater risk of anterograde amnesia than most other benzodiazepines .
145599	In 1991 and 1992 , the FDA emphasised the need for very short-term use and the fact that even 0.25 mg produced significantly more daytime anxiety than comparison drug or placebo .
145600	By contrast , R. H. B. Conacher of Upjohn Ltd has stated that in clinical trials various behavioural side-effects such as nervousness ‘ occurred in patients receiving placebo at a rate indistinguishable from that in patients receiving Halcion ’ .
145601	Perhaps it is Upjohn that is being highly selective regarding evidence on serious psychiatric reactions to triazolam .
145602	SIR , — Dr Jonas questions the documentation in our petition to the FDA arguing that triazolam 's benefit-to-risk ratio is inadequate .
145603	Of the 157 references in that petition , 108 are specifically cited to a document .
145604	These include : 30 controlled studies , by sixteen different investigator groups ; 13 controlled studies indicating limited efficacy for 0.25 mg of triazolam ; 50 case-reports ; 8 reports of post-marketing surveillance data ; and 11 published reports of laboratory evidence on triazolam 's safety problems .
145605	These 108 references do not include 4 references in the petition that constitute meta-analyses or reviews of different aspects of triazolam 's adverse reactions , to which Jonas refers misleadingly as ‘ replications of the same study by Kales . ’
145606	Jonas also states that ‘ equipotent doses of triazolam and other hypnotics show that triazolam does not produce more amnesia or behavioural medical events than other benzodiazepines . ’
145607	However , the controlled studies we cited compared doses of benzodiazepines that were equipotent both in regard to efficacy and to the starting recommended doses proposed by the respective manufacturer and approved by the FDA .
145608	Upjohn 's treatment , over the years as adverse reaction reports have accumulated , of the starting dosage recommendations for triazolam is instructive .
145609	Upjohn first introduced triazolam in 1977 at a recommended starting dose of up to 1.0 mg .
145610	After the Netherlands ' 1980 ban , Upjohn lowered the starting dose to 0.5 mg .
145611	When France , Italy , and West Germany banned the 0.5 mg tablet , Upjohn again reduced the dose worldwide to 0.25 mg .
145612	Even this has proved unacceptable in several countries , including the UK ( ban ) and France and Spain ( reduction to 0.125 mg ) .
145613	There have been sixteen drug regulatory actions worldwide against triazolam since 1980 aimed at the manufacturer 's recommended doses .
145614	Every time Upjohn denied the safety concerns yet subsequently reduced the dose .
145615	Stillbirth risk in Japan
145616	SIR , — Of a total of 3715,762 infants delivered in Japan after 23 weeks of gestation over the three years 1989 to 1991 , 22,531 were stillborn .
145617	Stillbirths account for about two-thirds of the perinatal deaths in Japan .
145618	We calculated the ‘ prospective risk of stillbirth ’ at week N , a newly proposed statistic , as : ( number of stillbirths at or beyond gestational week N ) ( number of total births at or beyond gestational week N ) 1000 .
145619	The figure shows the prospective risk of stillbirth at 23–42 weeks ' gestation for all births in Japan and the cumulative percentage of stillbirths .
145620	The risk at 23 weeks was about 6 per 1000 , indicating that 1 in 165 pregnant women will subsequently deliver a stillborn infant .
145621	The risk decreased by 39 weeks ' gestation to about 1.1 per 1000 ( 1 in 909 ) .
145622	Thereafter the risk increased progressively reaching more than 3 per 1000 at or beyond 42 weeks .
145623	A nearly constant fraction of fetuses that are alive at 23 weeks ' gestation die each subsequent week , indicating that every fetus faces a random , but statistically predictable , risk of intrauterine death throughout pregnancy .
145624	Despite antepartum fetal surveillance regimens , 28% of stillbirths ( about 2000 per year ) occur after 36 weeks of gestation .
145625	More than three-quarters of all stillbirths after 36 weeks were linked to unfavourable antepartum or intrapartum conditions and were free from fetal malformations .
145626	Consequently , the lives of more than 1500 mature and possibly healthy fetuses are lost in Japan each year .
145627	Their lives may be saved by either an appropriate mode of delivery or by ending the pregnancy at an appropriate gestational age — the optimal time for delivery ( the earliest date in a given pregnancy at which birth would carry a higher probability of healthy survival than would continued gestation ) .
145628	Our figures on the risk of stillbirth by gestational age strengthen the concept that , especially from the fetuses ' perspective , there is a biologically optimal time for delivery .

145646	Artemether in cerebral malaria
145647	SIR , — The possibility that observer bias may compromise an unblinded study must always be seriously considered .
145648	Dr Anstry ( April 17 , p 1035 ) raises this concern about our study of intramuscular artemether versus intravenous quinine as treatment for severe paediatric malaria .
145649	An unblinded design was necessary for this study , since artemether is commercially available only as an intramuscular injection , but intravenous quinine remains the treatment of choice for cerebral malaria in children .
